current_recipe.title: 3 Ingredient Biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and line a tray. Mix the flour and the pinch of salt in a bowl.
Stir in the cold cream with a fork until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
Pat the dough out on a floured surface to 2.5 cm thick, fold in half once and pat out again. Cut 8 rounds, pressing straight down.
Place the biscuits touching on the tray and brush the tops with the melted butter.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden. Serve warm.
current_recipe.description: Tall, tender cream biscuits made with just self-raising flour, double cream and butter, baked for 15 minutes at 220C.
tips: Keep the cream cold.
Fold only once and do not twist the cutter.
Bake the biscuits touching each other.
current_recipe.storage: Best the day they are made. Reheat for 5 minutes at 180C.

current_recipe.title: 3 Ingredient Fudge
steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and condensed milk in a heavy pan over very low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour into the tin, smooth the top and sprinkle with the flaky salt.
Leave to set for 2 hours, then cut into 24 squares with a hot knife.
current_recipe.description: Dark chocolate chips and condensed milk melted together with vanilla and set in a tin for 2 hours into smooth squares.
tips: Melt over very low heat.
Stir constantly to avoid catching.
Cut with a hot knife.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin for 2 weeks.

current_recipe.title: 5 Ingredient Chili
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the mince and brown for 8 minutes, breaking it up.
Stir in the chili powder and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and beans and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste, adjust the seasoning, and serve hot.
current_recipe.description: Beef mince, kidney beans, tinned tomatoes, onion and chili powder simmered for 35 minutes into a thick chili with only five ingredients.
tips: Use a generous amount of chili powder.
Brown the mince properly.
Simmer uncovered if the chili is too loose.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Abbacchio alla Scottadito
steps: Rub the cutlets with the oil, garlic, rosemary and pepper. Leave for 10 minutes.
Heat a griddle or grill to very hot.
Salt the cutlets and cook for 4 minutes on each side, in two batches, until browned outside and pink inside.
Rest for 2 minutes and serve with the lemon.
current_recipe.description: Tiny Roman lamb chops seasoned with rosemary, garlic and lemon and grilled for 15 minutes, eaten straight from the pan.
tips: Salt just before cooking.
Work in batches so the pan stays hot.
Eat with your fingers while they are hot.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Apple Chips
ingredients: 3 firm apples, cored and sliced 2 mm thick
steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice, then pat very dry. Mix the cinnamon and sugar and sprinkle over the slices.
Heat the air fryer to 150°C. Lay the slices in a single layer, in batches if needed.
Cook for 15 minutes, turning once, until dry and lightly golden at the edges.
Lift onto a rack and cool for 5 minutes, when they will crisp.
current_recipe.description: Thin apple slices dusted with cinnamon and cooked in the air fryer until dry and crisp. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Slice very thin and evenly for the best crunch.
Do not overlap the slices.
Check at 10 minutes if your machine runs hot.
Store in an airtight tin once fully cold.
current_recipe.storage: Keep in an airtight tin for up to 3 days; they soften if left uncovered.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Chickpeas
ingredients: 480 g tinned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
steps: Spread the drained chickpeas on a clean tea towel and rub dry. Leave for 10 minutes. Heat the air fryer to 190°C.
Toss the chickpeas with the oil, paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Cook for 15 minutes, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Tip onto a plate and cool for 5 minutes; they firm up as they cool.
current_recipe.description: Tinned chickpeas dried well, tossed in oil and spices and cooked in the air fryer until crunchy. Four servings in 20 minutes.
tips: Dry the chickpeas thoroughly before adding oil.
Shake the basket often for even crunch.
Store in an open bowl, not an airtight tin, or they soften.
Check at 12 minutes if your machine runs hot.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten on the day. Keep uncovered for up to 1 day; they soften in a sealed container.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Corn Ribs
ingredients: 3 corn cobs, about 900 g, husks removed
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C. Cut each cob in half crossways, stand each half on its flat end and cut downwards into 4 strips.
Toss the strips with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Cook in a single layer for 15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, until the edges are charred and the strips have curled.
Scatter with the Parmesan and squeeze over the lime. Serve hot.
current_recipe.description: Corn cobs cut into long strips that curl into ribs, then cooked in the air fryer with paprika and lime until charred.
tips: Use a sharp, heavy knife and a stable board.
Cook in batches so the ribs brown rather than steam.
Serve with extra lime and a dipping sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Donuts
steps: Mix the flour, yogurt and the 2 tablespoons of sugar into a soft dough. Roll out on a floured surface to 1.5 cm thick.
Cut 8 rounds with a 7 cm cutter and a small hole in each centre. Heat the air fryer to 180°C.
Cook in two batches for 8 minutes each, turning once, until golden.
Brush with the butter while hot and roll in the 60 g of sugar mixed with the cinnamon.
current_recipe.description: Biscuit dough rings cooked in the air fryer, then brushed with butter and rolled in cinnamon sugar. Makes 8 in 23 minutes.
tips: Do not knead the dough, or the donuts turn tough.
Cook in batches so the rings do not stick together.
Brush with the butter while hot so the sugar clings.
Check at 6 minutes if your machine runs hot.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten on the day. They keep in an airtight tin for 1 day and lose their softness.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Empanadas
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, cumin, paprika and salt. Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned and dry. Stir in the olives and egg and cool completely.
Heat the air fryer to 180C. Place a heaped tablespoon of filling on each disc, fold over and seal the edge with a fork.
Brush the empanadas with the beaten egg. Cook 4 at a time in the basket for 12 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving, as the filling stays very hot.
current_recipe.description: Beef and onion empanadas made with ready-rolled pastry discs, crimped by hand and air fried for 12 minutes until golden and crisp.
tips: Cool the filling fully before filling the pastry.
Press out any air from the parcel before sealing.
Prick each empanada once with a fork to let steam out.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat in the air fryer for 5 minutes at 160C.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Fish Fingers
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C for 3 minutes.
Arrange the fish fingers from frozen in a single layer in the basket, in two batches if needed.
Cook for 12 minutes, turning once halfway, until the coating is golden and crisp.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes. Butter the bread, make sandwiches with the fish fingers and tartare sauce, and serve with the peas and lemon.
current_recipe.description: Frozen fish fingers cooked straight from the freezer in the air fryer until crisp and golden. Four servings in 17 minutes.
tips: Cook from frozen; thawing makes the coating soggy.
Keep the fingers in one layer for an even crust.
Check one at 9 minutes if your machine runs hot.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Do not refreeze fish fingers once cooked unless the pack says it is safe.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Garlic Bread
steps: Mix the butter, garlic, parsley and salt. Heat the air fryer to 180°C.
Split the baguette lengthways and cut each half into pieces that fit the basket.
Spread the garlic butter over the cut sides, right to the edges.
Cook cut side up for 8 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges. Cut into slices and serve hot.
current_recipe.description: A halved baguette spread with garlic butter and parsley and cooked in the air fryer until crisp. Four servings in 13 minutes.
tips: Spread the butter right to the edges for a crisp crust.
Check at 6 minutes if your machine runs hot.
Add grated cheese for the last 2 minutes if you like.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Unbaked garlic bread freezes for up to 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Green Beans
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C. Dry the green beans well and toss them with the oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Cook the beans in a single layer in the basket for 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, until blistered and tender-crisp.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve.
current_recipe.description: Green beans cooked in the air fryer until blistered and tender-crisp with garlic and a squeeze of lemon. Four servings in 15 minutes.
tips: Choose beans of similar thickness so they cook at the same rate.
If your beans are very thick, add a minute or two and check one.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes with the oil for a little heat.
current_recipe.storage: Best straight away. Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days; re-crisp in the air fryer.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Grilled Cheese
steps: Heat the air fryer to 190C. Spread the butter on one side of each slice of bread.
Turn two slices buttered side down and spread with the mustard. Pile on the cheddar and mozzarella.
Top with the other slices, buttered side up. Press down lightly.
Air fry for 4 minutes, flip carefully and cook for 4 minutes more until golden and the cheese is melted.
Rest for 1 minute, then cut in half and serve.
current_recipe.description: Buttered sourdough filled with cheddar and mozzarella, air fried for 8 minutes until the bread is golden and the cheese has melted.
tips: Grate the cheese for a faster, more even melt.
Weigh down the top slice if it lifts in the airflow.
Add a slice of tomato or ham between the cheese for variety.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight from the fryer. It does not reheat well.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Hash Browns
steps: Grate the potatoes on the coarse side of a grater and squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean tea towel. Heat the air fryer to 190°C.
Mix the potato with the onion, flour, salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon of the oil, stirring in any starch left at the bottom of the bowl.
Press into 8 flat patties about 1.5 cm thick and brush with the remaining oil.
Cook in batches for 15 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
current_recipe.description: Grated potato squeezed dry, shaped into patties and cooked in the air fryer until crisp and golden. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Squeeze the grated potato until almost dry.
Keep the patties thin so they crisp through.
Check at 12 minutes if your machine runs hot.
Cook in batches rather than overlapping the patties.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in the air fryer at 190°C for 5 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Lamb Chops
steps: Take the chops out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Mix the olive oil, garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper and rub over both sides.
Heat the air fryer to 200C.
Place the chops in a single layer in the basket. Cook for 10 minutes, turning them over after 5 minutes. A thermometer should read 54C for medium-rare.
Transfer to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with the lemon wedges.
current_recipe.description: Lamb loin chops rubbed with garlic, rosemary and olive oil and air fried for 10 minutes, then rested until pink and juicy in the middle.
tips: Check with a thermometer at 8 minutes.
Pat the chops dry before rubbing them with oil.
Press the fat edge against the basket for a minute to crisp it.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep for 2 days in the fridge and are good cold in a salad.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Meatballs
steps: Stir the breadcrumbs into the milk and leave for 5 minutes. Heat the air fryer to 190°C.
Add the beef, pork, egg, garlic, oregano, salt, pepper and parmesan and mix gently until just combined. Shape into 20 balls with wet hands.
Arrange the meatballs in a single layer in the basket, in two batches if they do not fit, leaving a small gap between each.
Cook for 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until browned and cooked through. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.
current_recipe.description: Beef and pork meatballs with breadcrumbs, egg and garlic, cooked in a single layer in the air fryer until browned. Four servings in 27 minutes.
tips: Cook in batches rather than piling the meatballs up.
If your air fryer runs hot, check at 9 minutes.
Wet your hands when shaping so the mixture does not stick.
Cut one open to check that no pink remains.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in the air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes. Cooked meatballs freeze for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Onion Rings
ingredients: 2 large onions, cut into 1.5 cm slices
steps: Separate the onion slices into rings. Mix the flour, paprika and half the salt on a plate. Put the eggs in a shallow bowl and the panko with the rest of the salt on another plate.
Dip each ring in the flour, then the egg, then press firmly into the panko.
Heat the air fryer to 190°C. Brush the coated rings lightly with the oil.
Cook in single-layer batches for 10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Thick onion slices in a seasoned flour and breadcrumb coating, cooked in the air fryer until golden. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Press the crumbs on firmly so they stay put.
Brush with oil; a dry coating stays pale.
Cook in batches so the rings are not stacked.
Check at 7 minutes if your air fryer is a hot one.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Reheat in the air fryer at 190°C for 3 minutes to bring back some crispness.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Pizza Rolls
ingredients: 150 g low-moisture mozzarella, cut into small cubes
4 tbsp pizza sauce, warmed, for dipping
steps: Mix the mozzarella, pepperoni, 4 tbsp pizza sauce and oregano in a bowl.
Lay a wrapper in a diamond shape. Put 1 heaped tablespoon of filling in the centre. Wet the edges with water, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Heat the air fryer to 190C. Brush the rolls with the olive oil.
Cook in a single layer for 10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Rest for 2 minutes and serve with the warm pizza sauce for dipping.
current_recipe.description: Pizza rolls filled with mozzarella and pepperoni, sealed in egg roll wrappers and air fried for 10 minutes until crisp and bubbling.
tips: Do not overfill, or the cheese will burst through the seam.
Seal the edges firmly with water.
Make a batch and freeze the uncooked rolls on a tray.
current_recipe.storage: Uncooked rolls freeze for 1 month; cook from frozen with 3 extra minutes. Cooked ones keep for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Quesadilla
ingredients: 2 large flour tortillas, about 70 g each
100 g cheddar and mozzarella mix, grated
steps: Heat the air fryer to 190C. Mix the chicken, pepper, spring onion and cumin.
Lay a tortilla flat. Cover one half with half the cheese, half the chicken mixture, and top with more cheese. Fold over the other half.
Brush both sides lightly with the olive oil.
Air fry one quesadilla at a time for 8 minutes, turning once, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Rest for 1 minute, cut into wedges and serve with salsa and soured cream.
current_recipe.description: Flour tortillas filled with chicken, peppers and cheese, folded and air fried for 8 minutes until crisp and golden.
tips: Grate the cheese yourself for a smoother melt.
Do not overfill: a thin layer cooks through faster.
Use a small trivet on top if the tortilla lifts.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep for 1 day and reheat in the air fryer for 3 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Steak
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Heat the air fryer to 200°C for 3 minutes.
Pat the steaks dry, rub with the oil and season with the salt and pepper.
Lay them in the basket with space between and cook for 4 minutes. Turn and cook for 4 minutes more for medium.
Lift onto a plate, top with the butter, cover with foil and rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
current_recipe.description: Two steaks seasoned with salt and pepper, cooked in a very hot air fryer and rested under foil. Two servings in 15 minutes.
tips: Let the steaks come up to room temperature before cooking.
Pat the surface dry so it browns rather than steams.
If the steaks are thinner than 2.5 cm, check at 6 minutes.
A thermometer gives a far more reliable result than timing alone.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftover steak keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days and is good cold in a sandwich.

current_recipe.title: Air Fryer Turkey Breast
ingredients: 1 kg boneless turkey breast, skin on
steps: Mix the butter, garlic, thyme, sage, salt and pepper. Loosen the skin of the turkey and spread half of the butter underneath. Rub the rest over the top.
Heat the air fryer to 170C. Brush the basket with the olive oil.
Place the turkey skin side up in the basket. Cover loosely with foil and cook for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and cook for 20 minutes more, until the skin is golden and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 71C.
Rest under foil for 15 minutes, then slice against the grain.
current_recipe.description: A boneless turkey breast rubbed with butter and herbs, air fried for 50 minutes and rested until juicy, with crisp golden skin.
tips: Use a thermometer: 71C in the thickest part is cooked.
If the skin browns too fast, tent it with foil again.
Slice across the grain for tender portions.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Slice before storing and reheat gently with a splash of stock.

current_recipe.title: Ajoblanco
ingredients: 100 g stale white bread, crusts removed
steps: Soak the bread in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze it dry.
Blend the almonds, bread, garlic, 80 ml of the oil, vinegar and salt, adding the water a little at a time, for 3 minutes until very smooth.
Chill for 2 hours. Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Serve in small bowls with the grapes and the remaining oil.
current_recipe.description: A chilled Andalusian soup of blended almonds, bread, garlic, olive oil and sherry vinegar, served with grapes: 15 minutes of work, then 2 hours in the fridge.
tips: Use only one small garlic clove.
Blend until completely smooth.
Season again once chilled.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Antipasto Skewers
ingredients: 80 g jarred roasted red peppers, drained
steps: Pat the artichokes, peppers and olives dry. Fold the salami slices.
Thread the salami, mozzarella, olives, artichoke and pepper onto 8 skewers, alternating colours.
Arrange on a platter. Just before serving, drizzle with the oil and balsamic vinegar and scatter with the oregano.
current_recipe.description: Salami, mozzarella balls, olives, artichoke hearts and roasted peppers threaded onto skewers with a drizzle of oil and balsamic.
tips: Pat the jarred items dry.
Alternate the colours.
Dress just before serving.
Make up to 3 hours ahead.
current_recipe.storage: Best on the day. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day, undressed.

current_recipe.title: Appalachian Soup Beans
steps: Put the beans, ham hock, chopped onion, bay leaf and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook with the lid slightly ajar for 100 minutes, topping up with hot water if needed, until the beans are soft.
Add the salt and pepper. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot and simmer for 15 minutes more.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat and return it to the pot. Remove the bay leaf. Serve with the raw onion and vinegar.
current_recipe.description: Pinto beans simmered with a smoked ham hock and onion until soft and creamy, served with cornbread and raw onion.
tips: Add the salt late; early salt can toughen the skins.
Top up with hot water, not cold, if the pot gets dry.
Check a bean for tenderness before adding salt.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days and freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Apple Slice
ingredients: 4 apples, about 600 g, peeled and diced
2 tbsp caster sugar for the filling
100 g plain flour for the topping
60 g cold butter, cubed, for the topping
60 g caster sugar for the topping
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 cm square tin. Rub the 125 g butter into the 225 g flour and 60 g sugar, stir in the egg and press into the tin.
Cook the apples with the 2 tbsp sugar and cinnamon in a pan for 8 minutes until soft and dry. Cool slightly.
Rub the topping butter into the topping flour and sugar, then stir in the oats.
Spread the apple over the base, scatter the crumble on top and bake for 35 minutes until golden. Cool in the tin before cutting.
current_recipe.description: A buttery shortcrust base layered with stewed apple and topped with an oat crumble, baked and cut into squares.
tips: Cook the apple until it is dry.
Scatter the topping loosely.
If your oven runs hot, check at 28 minutes.
Cool before cutting.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Baingan Masala
ingredients: 2 aubergines, about 600 g, cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Toss the aubergine with the 1 tsp salt and leave for 15 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide pan over a high heat. Add the aubergine and cook for 8 minutes, turning, until browned. Remove.
Add the remaining oil and the cumin seeds, then the onion, and cook for 6 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Return the aubergine with the water, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes. Stir in the garam masala and coriander.
current_recipe.description: Aubergine pieces cooked with onion, tomato, ginger and ground spices until soft, with a thick sauce that clings.
tips: Do not skip salting if your aubergines are large.
Keep the pieces even so they cook together.
Add a splash of water if the sauce looks dry.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat gently.

current_recipe.title: Baked Beans from Scratch
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, beans, water and salt and bring to the boil.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste and adjust the sugar, vinegar or salt.
current_recipe.description: Haricot beans simmered in a sweet and smoky tomato sauce with onion, garlic and a splash of vinegar.
tips: Rinse the beans before they go in.
Simmer without a lid so the sauce thickens.
Taste at the end and adjust the sweetness and sharpness.
Add a splash of water if the sauce gets too thick.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days. Freezes well for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Banoffee Cheesecake
steps: Mix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter and press firmly into the base of a 23 cm springform tin.
Spread the caramel over the base and top with half the banana slices.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar until smooth. Whip 250 ml of the cream to soft peaks, fold it in and spread over the bananas.
Chill for 4 hours. Whip the remaining cream, spread it on top and finish with the remaining banana and the grated chocolate.
current_recipe.description: A no-bake cheesecake of biscuit base, cream cheese filling, toffee and sliced banana, finished with whipped cream and chocolate.
tips: Press the base down hard.
Slice the bananas at the last minute.
Do not overbeat the cream cheese.
Chill for the full 4 hours.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

current_recipe.title: BBQ Salmon
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skin on, about 600 g
steps: Heat the barbecue until very hot. Scrape clean and wipe with an oiled cloth.
Stir the brown sugar, mustard, soy sauce and garlic into a glaze.
Lay the salmon skin-side down, brush the flesh with the oil, close the lid and cook for 8 minutes.
Brush on the glaze and cook for 3 minutes more until the fish flakes. Serve with the lemon wedges.
current_recipe.description: Salmon fillets brushed with a brown sugar and mustard glaze and cooked on the barbecue until just flaking.
tips: Oil the grill.
Do not turn the fish.
Add the glaze at the end.
Check for flaking at 10 minutes.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Eat cold in a salad.

current_recipe.title: Bean and Rice Burrito
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice and cook for 2 minutes. Warm the refried beans in a separate pan or the microwave.
Warm the tortillas. Spread a quarter of the beans down the middle of each, then add the rice, salsa and cheese.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and toast seam side down in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.
current_recipe.description: Tortillas filled with spiced rice, refried beans, cheese and salsa, rolled and toasted in a pan. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Warm the tortillas first so they do not crack.
Do not overfill; fold in the ends before rolling.
Use leftover rice, cooked and cooled quickly.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days wrapped in foil. Reheat in a pan or oven at 180°C for 12 minutes. Freezes for up to 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Black Bean and Rice Skillet
ingredients: 480 g tinned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and rice and stir for 1 minute. Add the cumin and chili powder.
Pour in the tomatoes and water, add the beans, sweetcorn and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender.
Scatter with the cheese, cover for 2 minutes until melted, and serve.
current_recipe.description: Rice, black beans, tomatoes and sweetcorn cooked together in a spiced skillet and topped with cheese. Four servings in 35 minutes.
tips: Rinse the rice so the grains stay separate.
Keep the lid on tight; steam cooks the rice.
If the rice is firm after 15 minutes, add a splash of water and cook for 5 more.
current_recipe.storage: Cool quickly and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat until steaming throughout. Do not leave cooked rice out for more than an hour.

current_recipe.title: Bounty Slice
steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with paper. Mix the coconut and condensed milk to a thick paste.
Press it firmly into the tin and chill for 2 hours until firm.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil, spread over the top and chill for 30 minutes more.
Cut into 16 squares with a hot knife.
current_recipe.description: A no-bake slice of coconut and condensed milk set in the fridge and topped with dark chocolate. Sixteen servings in 2 hours 45 minutes, chilling included.
tips: Press the base firmly.
Chill until completely firm.
Cut with a hot knife.
Cut small pieces.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight tin for up to 1 week.

current_recipe.title: Brisket with Onions
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Season the brisket with the salt and pepper and brown it well in the oil on both sides, about 10 minutes.
Spread the onions and garlic in a deep pot, set the brisket on top and add the tomato purée, stock and bay leaves.
Cover tightly and cook for 3 hours 30 minutes until a fork slides in with no resistance.
Rest the brisket for 20 minutes, then slice across the grain and spoon over the onions and juices.
current_recipe.description: A beef brisket braised for three and a half hours on a bed of sliced onions with stock and tomato until tender.
tips: Brown the meat well.
Keep the lid tightly sealed.
If your oven runs hot, check at 3 hours.
Slice across the grain.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. It is easier to slice cold, then reheat in the juices.

current_recipe.title: Butter Chicken Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, garam masala and paprika for 2 minutes.
Add the passata, chicken and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick. Stir in the cream and cool for 15 minutes.
Spoon into a 1.5 litre pie dish, cover with the pastry, press the edge, brush with egg and cut a steam hole.
Bake for 20 minutes until risen and deep gold.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thigh in a creamy tomato and garam masala sauce under a puff pastry lid.
tips: Make the sauce thick.
Cool the filling before the pastry goes on.
If your oven runs hot, check at 16 minutes.
Add the cream at the end.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven for 20 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Cabbage and Potato Soup
steps: Melt the first measure of butter in a large pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 10 minutes until soft but still green.
Crush a few potatoes against the side of the pan to thicken the soup. Stir in the second measure of butter, the salt and the pepper.
current_recipe.description: Shredded cabbage, potatoes and onion simmered in stock until the potatoes thicken the broth, finished with butter.
tips: Cut the potatoes evenly so they cook at the same pace.
Add the cabbage late so it keeps its colour.
Crush a few potatoes for body rather than adding flour.
If the broth is too thick, loosen it with a little water.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat gently; the potatoes thicken it further as it cools.

current_recipe.title: Cabbage Salad with Peanut Dressing
ingredients: 2 carrots, about 150 g, cut into matchsticks
1 red pepper, about 150 g, cut into matchsticks
steps: Stir the peanut butter with the lime juice, soy sauce, honey and ginger, then add the water a spoon at a time until pourable.
Toss the cabbage, carrots, pepper and coriander with the dressing and leave for 5 minutes.
Scatter with the peanuts and serve cold.
current_recipe.description: Shredded cabbage, carrot and red pepper with coriander and peanuts, dressed with peanut butter, lime and soy sauce.
tips: Add the water gradually.
Shred the cabbage finely.
Let it stand for 5 minutes.
Add the peanuts last.
current_recipe.storage: Best on the day. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Cakey Brownies
ingredients: 80 g butter, softened, for the frosting
30 g cocoa powder, for the frosting
steps: Heat the oven to 175C. Grease and line a 20 cm square tin.
Whisk the melted butter, caster sugar, eggs and vanilla for 2 minutes until thick.
Sift in the flour, 40 g cocoa, baking powder and salt. Fold in with the milk until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake for 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the soft butter, icing sugar, 30 g cocoa and 2 tbsp milk until fluffy. Spread over the brownies and cut into 12.
current_recipe.description: Light, soft brownies with a cake-like crumb and a deep chocolate flavour, baked for 30 minutes and finished with chocolate frosting.
tips: Sift the cocoa to avoid lumps.
Cool completely before frosting.
Use a hot, dry knife to cut squares.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Cannelloni
ingredients: 300 g spinach, cooked and squeezed dry
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Mix the spinach with the ricotta, parmesan, egg, nutmeg and salt.
Stir the passata with the garlic and oregano and spread a third over the base of a baking dish.
Pipe the filling into the dried tubes and lay them in a single layer in the dish.
Pour over the rest of the tomato sauce so that every tube is covered, then the bechamel, and scatter with the mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 15 minutes more until golden.
current_recipe.description: Pasta tubes filled with ricotta and spinach, covered in tomato sauce and bechamel and baked until golden.
tips: Pipe the filling in.
Squeeze the spinach dry.
Cover the tubes with sauce.
If your oven runs hot, check at 35 minutes.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat covered until hot all the way through.

current_recipe.title: Carrot Cake Loaf
steps: Heat the oven to 175C. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Whisk the eggs, brown sugar and oil. Fold in the dry ingredients, then the carrots, walnuts and sultanas.
Pour into the tin and bake for 55 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, icing sugar and lemon juice until smooth. Spread over the loaf.
current_recipe.description: A moist spiced carrot loaf with walnuts and sultanas, baked for 55 minutes and topped with cream cheese icing.
tips: Grate the carrots finely.
Toast the walnuts for better flavour.
Ice only when the loaf is completely cool.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days with the icing.

current_recipe.title: Chantilly
steps: Chill a bowl and whisk in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Pour in the cream and whisk slowly, speeding up as it thickens.
Add the icing sugar and vanilla and whisk to soft peaks.
Use at once.
current_recipe.description: Cold double cream whipped with a little icing sugar and vanilla into soft peaks, ready in 5 minutes with no cooking.
tips: Chill the bowl, whisk and cream.
Stop whisking at soft peaks.
Use icing sugar, which dissolves quickly.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Keeps for 1 day covered in the fridge; whisk briefly to refresh.

current_recipe.title: Charoset
ingredients: 4 apples, about 600 g, peeled, cored and finely chopped
steps: Toss the chopped apples with the lemon juice.
Mix in the walnuts, wine, cinnamon and honey.
Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Chill for 1 hour before serving.
current_recipe.description: A sweet, chunky paste of chopped apples, walnuts, cinnamon and sweet red wine, eaten at the Passover seder to recall the mortar of the Israelites.
tips: Chop by hand for the best texture.
Make it a few hours ahead.
Add dates for a Sephardic variation.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Cheddar Jalapeno Bread
ingredients: 150 g mature cheddar, cut into 1 cm cubes
2 fresh jalapeños, deseeded and finely chopped
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water and oil and mix to a dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Flatten the dough, scatter over the cheese and jalapeños, then fold and knead gently until mixed in.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape into a round and place on a lined tray. Heat the oven to 220C with a tray inside.
Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce to 200C and bake for 30 minutes more until deep golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
Cool on a rack for 30 minutes before slicing.
current_recipe.description: A yeasted loaf studded with cubes of mature cheddar and chopped fresh jalapeños, baked for 40 minutes.
tips: Cut the cheese into cubes, not shreds.
Pat the chillies dry.
Cool before slicing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days wrapped. Freeze sliced for 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Cheese and Egg Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a 23 cm tin with the pastry and cook blind for 10 minutes with baking beans.
Lower the oven to 180°C. Scatter the bacon, chopped egg and cheddar over the base.
Whisk the raw eggs with the cream, salt and pepper and pour over.
Cook for 30 minutes until the custard is just set.
Cool for 10 minutes before slicing.
current_recipe.description: A shortcrust pie of hard-boiled egg, cheddar and bacon set in a creamy custard and cooked for 40 minutes. Six servings in 1 hour 5 minutes.
tips: Cook the base blind first.
Leave a gap at the top of the tin for the custard.
If your oven runs hot, check at 25 minutes.
Cool before slicing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Serve cold or warm it gently.

current_recipe.title: Cheese Tortellini with Pesto
steps: Boil the tortellini in a large pan of salted water for 4 minutes. Save a mugful of the water and drain.
Warm the tomatoes in the oil in a wide pan for 2 minutes until beginning to burst.
Add the tortellini, pesto and a splash of the pasta water and toss gently.
Scatter with the parmesan and pine nuts and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Fresh cheese tortellini tossed with basil pesto, cherry tomatoes and parmesan.
tips: Boil gently.
Save some pasta water.
Toss gently.
Serve straight away.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Cheesy Cauliflower Casserole

conditions: made with a hard cheese made without animal rennet in place of the parmesan
Vegetarian.note: Vegetarian when made with a hard cheese made without animal rennet in place of the parmesan.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the cauliflower with the oil and salt on a large baking tray and roast for 15 minutes, until the edges are browned and the florets are almost tender.
Meanwhile, beat the yogurt, cream cheese, two-thirds of the cheddar, the spring onions, garlic powder, mustard and pepper together in a large bowl.
Tip the hot cauliflower into the bowl and fold until coated. Spoon into a baking dish and top with the remaining cheddar.
Mix the Parmesan, ground almonds and paprika and scatter over the top. Lower the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake for 15 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
current_recipe.description: Roasted cauliflower folded into a tangy cheddar, yogurt and cream cheese sauce under a crisp Parmesan and almond topping. Six servings in 45 minutes.
tips: Spread the cauliflower in one layer on the tray; a crowded tray steams instead of roasting.
If the yogurt mixture looks thin, drain the yogurt through a sieve for a few minutes first.
Cover the dish loosely with foil if the topping browns faster than the sauce bubbles.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven until bubbling.

current_recipe.title: Cheesy Potato Bake
ingredients: 1.2 kg potatoes, peeled and sliced 4 mm thick
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Butter a 2.5 litre baking dish.
Layer a third of the potatoes and onion in the dish, season, and sprinkle with a third of the cheese. Repeat twice, finishing with cheese.
Pour the milk around the edge so it comes about three quarters of the way up. Dot with the butter.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes. Uncover and bake for 20 minutes more until golden and a knife slides in easily. Rest for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Sliced potatoes layered with cheese and onion, baked in a seasoned milk until golden. Six servings in 1 hour 15 minutes.
tips: Slice the potatoes evenly so they cook at the same speed.
Pour the milk down the side of the dish, not over the top.
Cover with foil to prevent the top browning before the potatoes are cooked.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat covered at 180°C for 25 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Cheesy Rice Casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Mix the rice, onion, milk, stock, mustard powder, salt, pepper and two thirds of the cheese in a 2.5 litre baking dish.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover, stir once, scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 10 minutes more until golden and the rice is tender. Rest for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Rice baked with cheese, milk, onion and a little butter until golden on top. Six servings in 50 minutes.
tips: Measure the liquid exactly; it controls the texture.
Cover tightly with foil so the rice steams.
If the rice is firm at the end, add a splash of hot stock and bake for 10 minutes more.
current_recipe.storage: Cool quickly and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of milk until steaming throughout.

current_recipe.title: Chicken Reshmi Kebab
ingredients: 30 g cashew nuts, ground to a paste
steps: Mix the chicken, cashew paste, cream, butter, ginger and garlic paste, chilli, cardamom, pepper, salt and coriander. Work the mixture for 2 minutes until sticky.
Chill for 30 minutes.
With wet hands, shape the mixture around 8 oiled skewers into long kebabs, or form 12 small patties.
Brush a griddle pan or frying pan with oil and cook over a medium-high heat for 15 minutes, turning every 4 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.
current_recipe.description: Silky minced chicken kebabs with cream, cashew paste, green chilli and cardamom, cooked on skewers or in a pan until just firm.
tips: Keep your hands wet when shaping so the mixture does not stick.
If the kebabs fall off the skewer, chill the mixture a little longer.
Do not press the kebabs while they cook; the juices stay in if you leave them alone.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a pan with a little oil.

current_recipe.title: Chicken Roulade
ingredients: 100 g baby spinach, wilted and squeezed dry
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Beat each breast between baking paper to 1 cm thick and season with the salt, pepper and oregano.
Spread the spinach, mozzarella and sun-dried tomatoes over each, leaving a 2 cm border.
Roll up tightly from the short end and tie with string in two places.
Brown the rolls in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 5 minutes, turning.
Roast for 30 minutes until no pink remains, rest for 5 minutes, remove the string and slice.
current_recipe.description: Flattened chicken breasts rolled round spinach, mozzarella and sun-dried tomatoes, tied and roasted, then sliced into rounds.
tips: Beat the chicken to an even thickness.
Squeeze the spinach dry.
If your oven runs hot, check at 25 minutes.
Tie the rolls in two places.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Slice and reheat gently, covered, or serve cold in a sandwich.

current_recipe.title: Chicken Sausage Pasta
steps: Boil the penne for 10 minutes, drain and keep a mugful of the water.
Meanwhile fry the sliced sausages in a wide dry pan for 6 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the cream, and simmer for 2 minutes, scraping the pan.
Toss in the pasta, spinach, parmesan and pepper off the heat, loosening with pasta water until glossy.
Serve straight away.
current_recipe.description: Sliced chicken sausages, spinach and garlic tossed through pasta with a splash of cream and parmesan.
tips: Brown the sausages properly before adding anything.
Keep some pasta water.
Stir in the spinach off the heat.
Serve at once, because the sauce tightens as it cools.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water or milk to loosen the sauce.

current_recipe.title: Chocolate Smoothie
ingredients: 2 bananas, sliced and frozen, about 240 g
steps: Pour the milk into a blender.
Add the frozen banana slices, cocoa, peanut butter, honey, vanilla, salt and ice.
Blend on low for 20 seconds, then on high for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Taste and add a little more honey if needed.
Pour into 2 glasses and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: A thick, cold smoothie of banana, cocoa, peanut butter and milk, blended in 5 minutes with ice.
tips: Freeze the bananas overnight.
Put the liquid in the blender first.
Drink it straight away.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day but separates.

current_recipe.title: Chorizo and Potato Stew
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks
steps: Fry the chorizo in a large pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until the oil runs and the edges crisp.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes, stock and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cook, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Crush a few against the side of the pan.
Stir in the vinegar, scatter with the parsley and serve.
current_recipe.description: Spanish chorizo, potatoes, peppers and tomato simmered with smoked paprika into a thick, brick-red stew, finished with parsley.
tips: Use cooking chorizo, not the cured eating type.
Crush a few potatoes to thicken the stew.
Add vinegar at the end to lift the flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Churro Waffles
ingredients: 60 g butter, melted, for the batter
steps: Heat and grease the waffle iron. Whisk the flour, baking powder, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and salt.
Whisk the eggs, milk and 60 g melted butter into the flour until just combined.
Cook 4 waffles for 4 minutes each until deep gold.
Mix the coating sugar and cinnamon on a plate. Brush each hot waffle with the 30 g butter and roll it in the sugar.
Warm the chocolate sauce for 1 minute and serve beside the waffles for dipping.
current_recipe.description: Light waffles rolled in cinnamon sugar while hot and served with a pot of warm chocolate sauce.
tips: Coat the waffles while they are hot.
Cook to deep gold so the crust stays crisp.
If your iron runs hot, check at 3 minutes.
Cut into sticks for dipping.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days but the coating softens.

current_recipe.title: Coffee Ice Cream
ingredients: 40 g whole coffee beans, lightly crushed
steps: Heat the cream, milk and coffee beans to a simmer. Cover, turn off the heat and steep for 30 minutes. Strain, pressing on the beans.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and salt until pale. Reheat the cream to steaming, then whisk a ladle into the yolks, then a second, and tip back into the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until the custard coats the back of a spoon and reaches 80C. Stir in the vanilla.
Strain into a bowl and chill for 4 hours until completely cold.
Churn in an ice cream machine until thick. Freeze in a lidded container for 4 hours.
current_recipe.description: A rich custard ice cream infused with coffee beans, chilled for 4 hours, churned and frozen until scoopable.
tips: Steep the beans, do not boil them.
Cook the custard to 80C and no further.
Chill the base completely before churning.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the freezer for 2 weeks.

current_recipe.title: Cookie Dough Bites
ingredients: 200 g heat-treated plain flour, sold as ready to eat raw
steps: Beat the butter with the brown and caster sugars for 2 minutes. Beat in the milk and vanilla.
Stir in the heat-treated flour, salt and chocolate chips to a firm dough. Roll into 20 balls and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the dark chocolate in short bursts for 3 minutes, dip each ball and set on baking paper.
current_recipe.description: Small balls of eggless cookie dough made with flour sold as heat-treated and ready to eat raw, chilled and dipped in dark chocolate.
tips: Use flour sold as heat-treated and ready to eat raw; check the packet.
Add milk a teaspoon at a time if the dough is crumbly.
Keep the bites in the fridge.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Cornetti
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt. Add the 2 eggs, milk, butter, zests and vanilla and knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise for 2 hours until doubled.
Divide in two and roll each into a circle 3 mm thick. Cut each into 6 triangles and roll up from the wide end. Curve into crescents on two lined trays.
Leave to rise for 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 190C.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 20 minutes until deep gold.
Warm the jam and brush it over the cornetti while hot.
current_recipe.description: Soft Italian breakfast crescents of sweet enriched dough, risen twice and baked for 20 minutes until golden.
tips: Knead until smooth and elastic.
Tuck the tip under the cornetto so it does not unroll.
Brush with warm jam for a glossy finish.
current_recipe.storage: Best the day they are made. Freeze for 1 month.

current_recipe.title: Crispy Aromatic Duck
ingredients: 3 spring onions, cut into 5 cm lengths
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
6 spring onions, cut into fine strips
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C / 300°F. Prick the duck skin all over with a fork and rub the salt and five-spice into both sides.
Set the legs skin side up in a roasting tin with the ginger, the 3 lengths of spring onion and the star anise, and pour the soy sauce, wine and water around them, not over them.
Cover the tin tightly with foil and cook for 2 hours, until the meat is very tender and pulling away from the bone.
Lift the legs onto a wire rack set over a tray and leave them to cool and dry for 30 minutes. Keep the juices from the tin.
Turn the oven up to 220°C / 425°F and roast the legs on the rack, skin side up, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Warm the pancakes following the packet instructions.
Shred the duck meat and skin with two forks, discarding the bones, and pile it on a plate.
Serve with the pancakes, hoisin sauce, cucumber and spring onion strips, for everyone to fill and roll their own.
current_recipe.description: Duck legs cooked slowly with five-spice, ginger and star anise until they fall off the bone, then crisped in a hot oven and shredded for pancakes, hoisin, cucumber and spring onion.
current_recipe.imageQuery: Shredded crispy aromatic duck on a plate with warm Chinese pancakes, hoisin sauce, cucumber matchsticks and spring onion strips
tips: Keep the tin tightly covered for the long cooking. The trapped steam is what makes the meat tender, and a loose lid dries it out.
Let the legs cool and dry before they go back into the oven. Damp skin steams and turns leathery, but dry skin blisters and crisps.
Skim the fat from the tin juices and keep it. Duck fat makes the best roast potatoes, and the juices below it make a good base for a soup.
current_recipe.storage: The cooked legs keep in the fridge for up to 3 days before crisping, so the slow part can be done ahead. Crisped duck is best eaten at once. Keep the strained duck fat in the fridge for up to a month.

current_recipe.title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 3 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Set the potatoes on an oiled tray and press each flat with a glass to 1 cm thick.
Drizzle with the oil, scatter with the garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until deep gold and crisp.
current_recipe.description: Small potatoes boiled until tender, squashed flat and roasted in olive oil with garlic and rosemary until crisp.
tips: Let the potatoes steam dry.
Smash them gently so they stay in one piece.
If your oven runs hot, check at 24 minutes.
Do not crowd the tray.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Reheat leftovers in a 220°C oven for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Divinity
ingredients: 100 g pecans, roughly chopped, plus pecan halves to decorate
steps: Line two baking trays with baking parchment. Put the egg whites in the clean bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk.

Put the sugar, corn syrup and water in a heavy saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Clip a candy thermometer on the pan and cook without stirring until the syrup reaches 127°C / 260°F, the hard-ball stage, about 10 to 12 minutes.
When the syrup reaches about 120°C / 248°F, start whisking the egg whites on high speed until they form stiff peaks.
With the mixer running on medium speed, pour the hot syrup into the whites in a thin, steady stream, pouring against the side of the bowl. Add the vanilla.
Beat on high speed for 5 to 8 minutes, until the mixture loses its gloss, holds a peak and starts to look matt. Fold in the chopped pecans.

Working quickly, drop rounded teaspoons onto the trays with two spoons, swirling the tops into peaks, and press a pecan half on each. Leave to set at room temperature for 1 hour, until firm on the outside.
current_recipe.description: Airy, cloud-like Southern candy of sugar, corn syrup and whipped egg white, beaten until it holds its shape and studded with pecans. A Christmas tin favourite.
current_recipe.imageQuery: A plate of white, cloud-like divinity candies swirled into peaks, each topped with a pecan half, on a piece of baking parchment
tips: Make it on a dry day. Divinity will not set in humid weather, so check the forecast and pick a cool, dry day.
Pour the syrup in a thin stream, and do not scrape the pan. Crystals on the side of the pan can seed the whole batch and make it grainy.
Drop the candy as soon as the mixture loses its shine. If it is beaten too long, it stiffens in the bowl and cannot be shaped.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin, in layers with baking parchment, for up to 1 week. Do not refrigerate. It absorbs moisture and turns sticky in humid conditions.

current_recipe.title: Egyptian Rice with Vermicelli
ingredients: 60 g dried vermicelli, broken into short pieces
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pan over a medium heat. Add the vermicelli and fry for 3 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat in the butter.
Pour in the stock and salt and bring to the boil. Cover, lower the heat to the minimum and cook for 15 minutes.
Rest off the heat, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
current_recipe.description: Short grain rice cooked with golden-fried vermicelli pasta in stock, fluffy and savoury.
tips: Stir the vermicelli constantly while it browns.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Keep the lid on while the rice cooks.
Use water instead of stock for a plainer rice.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Epinards a la Creme
steps: Wilt the spinach in batches in a large dry pan over medium heat for 1 minute each. Tip into a colander, press out the liquid and chop roughly.
Melt the butter in the pan and cook the shallot for 2 minutes. Stir in the flour for 30 seconds.
Add the cream and nutmeg and simmer for 2 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Stir in the spinach, salt and pepper and warm through for 2 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Fresh spinach wilted in butter and finished in cream with a pinch of nutmeg, ready in 25 minutes.
tips: Squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Season with care; spinach needs salt.
Use fresh nutmeg for the best flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Keeps for 1 day in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Erbsensuppe
steps: Put the peas, ham hock, onions, carrots, celery, bay and water in a large pan and bring to the boil. Skim.
Simmer for 90 minutes, stirring often, until the peas fall apart.
Lift out the hock, pull off the meat and return it to the pot with the sausage and marjoram. Heat for 5 minutes.
Remove the bay, stir in the vinegar and pepper and thin with hot water if needed.
current_recipe.description: A thick German split pea soup with smoked pork and sausage simmered for 90 minutes until the peas fall apart.
tips: Stir often and scrape the base.
Add water to thin it when reheating.
Add the vinegar at the end to lift the flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Freeze for 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Freezer Cookie Dough
steps: Cream the butter and both sugars for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, then fold in the chocolate chunks.
Scoop 24 balls onto trays lined with baking paper and freeze for 2 hours until solid.
Move the frozen balls into a freezer bag and keep frozen.
To bake, heat the oven to 175C and place the frozen balls 5 cm apart on a lined tray. Bake for 14 minutes and cool for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Chocolate chip cookie dough scooped into balls and frozen for 2 hours, then baked straight from the freezer for 14 minutes.
tips: Freeze the balls on a tray first.
Bake from frozen, adding 2 minutes.
Label the bag with the date.
current_recipe.storage: The dough balls keep in the freezer for 3 months. Baked cookies keep for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Freezer Mac and Cheese

conditions: made with a hard cheese made without animal rennet in place of the gruyère
Vegetarian.note: Vegetarian when made with a hard cheese made without animal rennet in place of the gruyère.

steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Boil the macaroni for 3 minutes short of the pack time. Drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in the warm milk gradually. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, stir in the mustard, nutmeg, salt, cheddar and Gruyère until smooth. Stir in the macaroni.
Pour into a large dish, scatter with the breadcrumbs and bake for 20 minutes until golden.
Leave to cool, moving the dish to the fridge within 2 hours of baking, then cut into 8 portions and wrap each. Freeze for up to 3 months.
current_recipe.description: A baked macaroni cheese with cheddar and Gruyere, cooled and frozen in portions, then thawed overnight and reheated for 20 minutes.
tips: Use a flour-thickened sauce for stability.
Undercook the pasta.
Freeze in single portions.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the freezer for 3 months. Thaw overnight and reheat at 180C for 20 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Freezer Soup
steps: Heat the oil and fry the onions, carrots and celery for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock and salt and simmer for 35 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Cool quickly, ladle into tubs and freeze.
current_recipe.description: A thick vegetable and lentil soup simmered for 35 minutes, cooled and frozen in portions. Eight servings in 50 minutes.
tips: Leave out potatoes and pasta.
Cool the soup fast before freezing.
Leave room in the tubs.
Label every tub.
current_recipe.storage: Freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen over low heat until steaming hot.

current_recipe.title: Fried Cabbage
steps: Fry the bacon in a large deep pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Lift out, leaving the fat.
Add the butter and onion and cook for 4 minutes. Add the cabbage in batches and leave for 3 minutes before stirring.
Cook for 8 minutes in total, stirring now and then, until soft and browned at the edges.
Return the bacon, season with the salt and pepper, and stir in the vinegar.
current_recipe.description: Shredded cabbage fried in butter and bacon fat until soft and browned at the edges. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Use a wide pan so the cabbage fries rather than steams.
Add the cabbage in batches.
Season at the end; bacon is salty.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan.

current_recipe.title: Fried Egg Sandwich
steps: Toast the bread and spread one slice with the mayonnaise.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat and crack in the egg. Season with the salt, cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Lay the cheese on the egg, cover for 30 seconds until it melts.
Lift the egg onto the mayonnaise slice, add the lettuce and close with the second slice. Cut in half.
current_recipe.description: A fried egg with a runny yolk, melted cheese and a leaf of lettuce between two slices of toasted bread. One serving in 9 minutes.
tips: Cover the pan to set the top of the egg without flipping.
Add cheese straight after the egg is done to melt it.
Cook for 1 minute more if you prefer a firm yolk.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away.

current_recipe.title: Fruit Punch
steps: Stir the pineapple, orange and cranberry juices together in a large punch bowl.
Add the sliced oranges and strawberries.
Just before serving, pour in the lemonade and sparkling water and add the ice.
Stir gently and ladle into glasses with some fruit.
current_recipe.description: A party bowl of pineapple, orange and cranberry juice with lemonade, sparkling water and sliced fruit.
tips: Add the fizzy drinks at the last minute.
Keep everything cold.
Taste and adjust before serving.
Keep the bowl on ice in hot weather.
current_recipe.storage: Best on the day. Keeps the mixed juices in the fridge for 2 days.

current_recipe.title: Gänsebraten
ingredients: 2.3 kg goose meat and skin, from a 4.5 kg bird
steps: Heat the oven to 160C. Prick the goose skin all over. Rub inside and out with the salt, pepper and half the marjoram.
Fill the cavity with the apples, onions and the remaining marjoram.
Set breast up on a rack in a roasting tin with the water. Roast for 3 hours, pouring off the fat every 45 minutes.
Turn the oven to 220C and roast for 15 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Rest for 30 minutes under foil. Skim the tin juices, add the stock and cornflour mixed with water and simmer for 5 minutes for the gravy.
current_recipe.description: A whole goose roasted for 3 hours with apples, onions and marjoram until the skin is crisp, the German Christmas roast.
tips: Prick the skin without piercing the meat.
Pour off the fat during roasting.
Rest the goose for 30 minutes.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Save the goose fat for roasting.

current_recipe.title: Garlic Chicken Pasta
ingredients: 360 g skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Cook the penne in a large pan of unsalted boiling water for 10 minutes, until just tender. Save a mugful (about 250 ml) of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 6 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Tip onto a plate.
Lower the heat, add the remaining oil and the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until pale gold. Add the oregano, chilli flakes and pepper.
Return the chicken and pasta to the pan with the lemon juice and a splash of the pasta water. Toss for 1 minute, adding more water as needed. Stir in the parsley.
current_recipe.description: Penne tossed with seared chicken, sliced garlic, lemon, parsley and a little chilli in a light sauce made from pasta water and olive oil. Four servings in 30 minutes.
tips: Add the pasta water a little at a time; you may not need all of it.
Take the garlic off the heat at once if it starts to brown; bitter garlic spoils the dish.
Use a wide pan so that the pasta can be tossed without spilling.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Garlic Pull Apart Bread
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a 23 cm loaf tin. Cut the dough into 24 pieces and roll each into a ball.
Mix the butter, garlic, parsley and salt. Toss the dough balls in the butter until coated.
Pack the balls into the tin, scattering the mozzarella between the layers.
Bake for 25 minutes until deep gold. Brush with any remaining butter and serve hot.
current_recipe.description: Balls of pizza dough tossed in garlic butter and parsley, baked in a loaf tin and torn apart at the table.
tips: Coat every ball in the butter.
Pack the tin snugly.
If your oven runs hot, check at 20 minutes.
Serve it hot, straight from the tin.
current_recipe.storage: Best hot. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days and reheats in a 160°C oven for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Gluten-Free Chicken Nuggets
ingredients: 500 g chicken breast, cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and put a baking tray inside to heat.
Pat the chicken dry. Toss it with the cornflour and salt in a bowl until lightly coated.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the oil, paprika and garlic powder on a plate.
Dip each piece in the beaten egg, then press into the crumbs on all sides.
Lay the nuggets on the hot tray and bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
current_recipe.description: Chicken breast pieces coated in a cornflour, egg and gluten-free breadcrumb crust and baked for 15 minutes at 220C until crisp.
tips: Dry the chicken before coating, or the crust will slide off.
If your nuggets are bigger than 3 cm, add 3 minutes and check one.
Press the crumbs on firmly with the flat of your hand.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat on a tray at 200C for 8 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Gluten-Free Tortillas
steps: Mix the masa harina and salt in a bowl, add the warm water and knead for 2 minutes to a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. Press each between two sheets of baking paper to a round about 15 cm across.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook each tortilla for 1 minute, flip and cook for 1 minute more, then flip again for 30 seconds until it puffs.
Stack in a clean cloth to keep them warm and soft.
current_recipe.description: Soft corn tortillas made with masa harina and warm water, pressed thin and cooked on a hot dry pan.
tips: If the edges crack, add a spoonful of water to the dough.
Cook in a very hot, dry pan.
Wrap cooked tortillas in a cloth to steam.
current_recipe.storage: Best the day they are made. Reheat in a dry pan.

current_recipe.title: Grilled Romaine Salad
ingredients: 2 anchovy fillets, about 10 g, finely chopped
steps: Halve the romaine hearts lengthways, keeping the root. Rinse and dry very well and brush the cut sides with the oil.
Stir the mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic, anchovy, grated parmesan and water into a dressing.
Heat a grill or griddle pan until very hot. Lay the lettuce cut-side down for 2 to 3 minutes until charred, then turn for 1 minute.
Plate with the char facing up, spoon over the dressing and finish with the shaved parmesan and pepper.
current_recipe.description: Halved romaine hearts charred on a grill and dressed with a Caesar-style dressing, parmesan and lemon.
tips: Dry the lettuce well.
Use a very hot grill.
Keep the root intact.
Dress at the last moment.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away.

current_recipe.title: Ground Beef and Potato Skillet
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes in a single layer and leave for 6 minutes. Turn and cook for 8 minutes more until golden and tender.
Push the potatoes to the sides. Add the mince to the middle, break it up and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic powder and paprika and cook for 4 minutes, stirring everything together.
Season with the salt, scatter with the cheese and cover for 1 minute, only until it melts. Finish with the spring onions.
current_recipe.description: Diced potatoes crisped in a pan, then tossed with browned beef mince, onion and cheese. Four servings in 35 minutes from one skillet.
tips: Spread the potatoes in a single layer so they fry rather than steam.
If the potatoes stick, wait; they release once a crust forms.
Drain off excess fat from the mince before the onion goes in if the pan looks greasy.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot frying pan for 5 minutes to bring back the crust.

current_recipe.title: Ham and Cheese Sliders
ingredients: 12 soft sweet dinner rolls, joined in a sheet (about 500 g)
200 g sliced Swiss cheese, Emmental or Gruyère
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F (160°C fan) and grease a 23 x 33 cm baking dish.
Without separating the rolls, slice the whole sheet in half horizontally with a serrated knife. Set the bottom half in the dish and spread it with 1 tbsp of the mustard.
Layer the ham and then the cheese over the bottom half and put the top half of the rolls back on.

Whisk the melted butter with the remaining mustard, the Worcestershire sauce, sugar, poppy seeds, onion granules and garlic granules. Spoon it over the tops of the rolls and brush it into an even layer.
Cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for 10 minutes more, until the tops are golden and the cheese has melted.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into 12 sliders along the lines of the rolls and serve warm.
current_recipe.description: A tray of soft sweet rolls filled with ham and Swiss cheese, brushed with mustard, poppy seed and Worcestershire butter and baked until golden. Twelve sliders.
current_recipe.imageQuery: A tray of golden baked ham and cheese sliders on soft sweet rolls, glossy with a poppy seed and mustard butter and cut into squares, with melted Swiss cheese showing
tips: Keep the rolls joined and slice them in one pass with a long serrated knife. It saves time, and it keeps the filling and the top in place.
Cover the tray for the first half of baking. The foil keeps the tops from browning before the cheese in the middle has melted.
Make the glaze while the oven heats and pour it on just before baking. Butter left on the rolls for hours makes the tops greasy and the bottoms soft.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 160°C / 325°F (140°C fan) oven, covered with foil, for 12 minutes. Freezes for 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Ham and Egg Pie
ingredients: 300 g cooked gammon or ham, diced
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line a 23 cm deep dish with two thirds of the pastry and blind bake for 10 minutes.
Lower the oven to 190°C. Scatter the ham over the base, brush with the mustard and crack in the eggs, spacing them out. Season with the pepper.
Cover with the remaining pastry, crimp the edges, cut a slit and brush with the beaten egg.
Cook for 30 minutes until golden. Cool before slicing.
current_recipe.description: Gammon and whole eggs set in a shortcrust case under a lid and cooked for 40 minutes, served cold with chutney.
tips: Blind bake the base.
Space the eggs out.
If your oven runs hot, check at 25 minutes.
Cool before cutting.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days and is good cold.

current_recipe.title: Herb Burgers
ingredients: 440 g lean ground beef (90 per cent lean)
4 small burger buns, about 50 g each
40 g red onion, in thin rings
steps: Mix the beef, grated onion, parsley, thyme, garlic and pepper lightly with your hands until just combined.
Shape into 4 patties about 11 cm across and press a shallow dimple into the middle of each.
Heat a grill pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the patties for 6 minutes a side, until browned and the centres reach 71°C. Rest for 2 minutes.
Toast the buns for 30 seconds, spread with the mustard and fill with the lettuce, patties and red onion.
current_recipe.description: Lean beef burgers with parsley, thyme, garlic and grated onion, cooked in a pan and served in small buns with lettuce, red onion and mustard. Four servings in 22 minutes.
tips: Do not press on the patties while they cook; it squeezes out the juices.
Chill the shaped patties for 10 minutes if the kitchen is warm.
Keep the buns small; they are the largest source of sodium on the plate.
current_recipe.storage: Cooked patties keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. Raw patties can be frozen for up to 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Homemade Cola
steps: Simmer the sugar, water, orange zest, lime zest, cinnamon and cloves over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve and stir in the vanilla and lemon juice. Cool.
For each glass, pour about 40 ml of syrup over ice and top with 125 ml sparkling water.
current_recipe.description: A cola-style syrup of citrus zest, cinnamon, cloves, vanilla and brown sugar, mixed with sparkling water.
tips: Measure the cloves.
Add the vanilla off the heat.
Taste and adjust the strength.
Keep the sparkling water cold.
current_recipe.storage: The syrup keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

current_recipe.title: Honey Garlic Pork Chops
ingredients: 4 pork loin chops, about 180 g each
steps: Pat the chops dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and sear for 4 minutes per side. Lift out and rest.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the honey, soy sauce, vinegar and water and simmer for 3 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.
Return the chops and any juices to the pan and turn in the glaze for 1 minute. Serve with the sauce spooned over.
current_recipe.description: Pork chops seared in a pan and glazed with a sauce of honey, garlic and soy. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Add the glaze after the chops are cooked, because honey burns on a hot pan.
If the sauce reduces too far, loosen it with a spoonful of water.
Thin chops may cook in 3 minutes per side, so check early.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Hühnersuppe mit Nudeln
steps: Put the chicken in a large pot with the water and bring slowly to a bare simmer. Skim the foam.
Add the 2 whole carrots, celery, leek, onion and bay and simmer for 40 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth. Shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Return the broth to the pot with the diced carrot and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the meat, parsley, nutmeg and salt and serve.
current_recipe.description: A clear chicken soup with carrots, celery and fine noodles, made by simmering a whole chicken for 40 minutes.
tips: Start with cold water and bring it up slowly.
Skim the foam for a clear broth.
Cook the noodles separately for the clearest soup.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Freeze the broth for 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Beans and Ham
steps: Put the beans, ham hock, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaf, thyme and water in the Instant Pot.
Seal the lid and cook on high pressure for 50 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest.
Lift out the hock and pull the meat from the bone. Discard the skin, fat and bone and shred the meat.
Return the meat to the pot. Mash a few beans against the side to thicken the broth.
Stir in the vinegar and pepper, taste for salt and serve.
current_recipe.description: Dried beans cooked under pressure with a smoked ham hock, carrot, onion and celery until creamy, with the ham pulled through the pot.
tips: Do not add salt until after the hock has cooked.
Mash a ladleful of beans to thicken the broth.
Soak the beans for a softer result and a shorter cook.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Beef Bourguignon
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
steps: Season the beef with the salt and pepper. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and cook the lardons for 4 minutes. Remove them. Brown the beef in 2 batches in the olive oil for 4 minutes per batch.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scraping the base, and reduce for 5 minutes. Add the stock, thyme and lardons.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 35 minutes. Release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest.
Fry the mushrooms in 10 g of the butter until golden. Mash the remaining butter with the flour, stir into the stew on sauté for 3 minutes until thick, and fold in the mushrooms.
current_recipe.description: Beef chuck braised under pressure in red wine with bacon, mushrooms, onions and carrots until tender in a glossy sauce.
tips: Brown the beef in batches, not all at once.
Scrape the base of the pot clean before sealing.
Add the thickener at the end, not before pressure cooking.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Better the next day.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Beef Brisket
steps: Mix the paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper and rub all over the brisket. Cut the meat in half if it does not fit the pot.
Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Heat the olive oil and sear the brisket for 4 minutes on each side. Remove it.
Layer the onions and garlic in the pot. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and tomato purée and stir, scraping the base.
Return the brisket fat side up. Seal and cook on high pressure for 90 minutes. Release naturally for 20 minutes.
Rest the meat for 15 minutes in the liquid. Skim the fat, reduce the sauce on sauté for 10 minutes, slice the brisket against the grain and serve.
current_recipe.description: A beef brisket joint cooked under pressure with onions, garlic and stock for 90 minutes until tender enough to slice or shred.
tips: Slice against the grain for tender portions.
Cook fat side up so it bastes the meat.
Reduce the sauce after cooking for a rich finish.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge in its sauce, or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Beef Curry
ingredients: 600 g beef chuck, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Heat the oil and cook the onions for 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli. Stir for 1 minute, then add the beef and stir to coat.
Add the tomatoes, yogurt, salt and water, scraping the base.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 30 minutes. Release naturally for 10 minutes.
If the sauce is thin, simmer on sauté for 5 minutes. Stir in the garam masala and coriander.
current_recipe.description: Cubed beef chuck cooked under pressure in an onion, tomato and spice sauce until tender, finished with fresh coriander.
tips: Brown the onions fully: they are the flavour base.
Use little liquid because nothing evaporates under pressure.
Add the garam masala at the end.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Beef Stroganoff
ingredients: 500 g beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
steps: Season the beef with half of the salt. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and brown the beef in the oil in 2 batches for 3 minutes each. Remove.
Cook the onion and mushrooms for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, paprika and remaining salt, scraping the base. Add the noodles and press them under the liquid. Return the beef on top.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 5 minutes. Release the pressure quickly.
Stir well, switch off the heat and stir in the soured cream. Serve with the parsley.
current_recipe.description: Strips of beef cooked under pressure with mushrooms and onions, stirred through egg noodles with soured cream and mustard.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain in thin strips.
Stir in the soured cream after the heat is off.
Do not stir the noodles before sealing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Add a splash of stock when reheating as the noodles absorb liquid.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Butter Chicken
ingredients: 700 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Set the pot to sauté. Melt the first 2 tbsp butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic paste and spices and cook for 1 minute.
