Add the tomatoes, scraping the base to loosen any bits. Add the chicken and salt and do not stir.
Lock the lid and cook at high pressure for 8 minutes. Release the pressure naturally for 5 minutes, then manually.
Set to sauté on low. Stir in the remaining butter and the cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Crush the fenugreek leaves over the top and scatter with the coriander.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs pressure-cooked in a spiced tomato sauce, then finished with butter and cream for a rich, mild curry.
tips: Deglaze fully to avoid the burn warning.
Blend the sauce with a stick blender for a smoother texture.
Add the cream at the end; pressure can split it.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days and freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Chicken Cacciatore
ingredients: 8 chicken thighs, bone in, about 1 kg
steps: Season the chicken with the salt. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and brown the thighs in the oil, skin side down, for 6 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Cook the onion, peppers and mushrooms for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scrape the base and reduce for 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes, purée and oregano, then return the chicken.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes. Release naturally for 8 minutes.
Simmer on sauté for 5 minutes if the sauce is thin. Stir in the olives and basil.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs braised under pressure with peppers, onion, mushrooms and tomato, finished with olives and a splash of red wine.
tips: Brown the skin deeply for flavour.
Reduce the wine before adding the tomatoes.
Add olives and basil after cooking.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Chicken Thighs
steps: Rub the thighs with the salt, paprika, garlic powder and pepper. Set the pot to sauté, heat the oil and brown the thighs skin side down in two batches, 5 minutes each. Lift out.
Pour in the stock and scrape the base. Set the rack in the pot and the thighs on top.
Lock the pressure cooker lid and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 5 minutes.
Heat the grill to high. Lay the thighs skin side up on a tray and grill for 5 minutes until crisp. Spoon over the juices.
current_recipe.description: Bone-in chicken thighs seasoned and pressure cooked in 10 minutes, then crisped under the grill. Four servings in 35 minutes.
tips: Brown the skin first, then keep it above the liquid.
Finish under the grill for crisp skin.
Season at least 15 minutes before cooking.
Use the cooking juices as a sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat at 180°C for 12 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 600 g chicken thighs, boneless, cut into chunks
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, 1 tsp garam masala, turmeric, cumin, lemon juice and salt. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Brown the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes and remove it.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato purée, then stir for 1 minute. Add the passata and remaining garam masala.
Return the chicken. Seal and cook on high pressure for 6 minutes. Release naturally for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and crush the fenugreek leaves over the top. Simmer for 2 minutes and serve.
current_recipe.description: Spiced yogurt-marinated chicken pieces in a creamy tomato sauce, cooked under pressure and finished with cream and fenugreek.
tips: Add the cream after pressure cooking, never before.
Marinate for longer for more flavour.
Crush the fenugreek between your fingers to release its scent.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Chili
ingredients: 480 g tinned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Set the pot to sauté. Heat the oil and brown the mince for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, beans, purée, water and salt. Scrape the base of the pot so nothing sticks.
Lock the pressure cooker lid, set the valve to sealing and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest. Stir, and use the sauté setting for 5 minutes if it is too thin.
current_recipe.description: Beef mince, beans, tomatoes and chili powder pressure cooked together until thick, in one pot. Six servings in 40 minutes.
tips: Scrape the base after sautéing, or the pot may give a burn warning.
Keep the liquid modest; the pot does not let it evaporate.
Taste for salt after pressure cooking.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming throughout.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Dal
steps: Rinse the dal in several changes of water until clear. Put it in the pot with the water, turmeric, tomato, salt and the oil.
Lock the lid and cook at high pressure for 10 minutes. Release naturally for 10 minutes. Whisk the dal until creamy, adding hot water if it is too thick.
Heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the cumin seeds, garlic, dried chillies and asafoetida and cook for 1 minute until the garlic is golden.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the dal, stir and add the coriander.
current_recipe.description: Yellow split lentils pressure-cooked until creamy and finished with a hot tempering of cumin, garlic and chilli.
tips: Add a splash of hot water if the dal thickens as it stands.
Do not skip the rinse; it removes foam-causing starch.
Add lemon juice at the end for brightness.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Lamb Shanks
steps: Season the shanks with the salt and pepper. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and brown the shanks in the oil for 4 minutes per side. Remove them.
Cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato purée and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scrape the base and reduce for 4 minutes. Add the stock, rosemary and bay leaves.
Return the shanks and seal. Cook on high pressure for 60 minutes. Release naturally for 15 minutes.
Lift out the shanks. Skim the fat, then reduce the sauce on sauté for 10 minutes. Spoon over the shanks.
current_recipe.description: Lamb shanks browned and cooked under pressure with red wine, garlic, rosemary and tomato until the meat slides off the bone.
tips: Brown the shanks well: this builds the flavour.
Skim the fat before reducing the sauce.
The meat is ready when it falls from the bone at a touch.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge in the sauce, or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Mac and Cheese
steps: Put the macaroni, water, mustard powder, salt and butter in the pot. Do not stir.
Lock the pressure cooker lid, set the valve to sealing and pressure cook on high for 4 minutes.
Release the pressure quickly. Stir, then add the milk and the cheese in handfuls, stirring until melted and creamy.
Season with the pepper and let it stand for 3 minutes to thicken.
current_recipe.description: Macaroni cooked in milk and stock under pressure, then stirred with cheddar into a creamy sauce. Four servings in 15 minutes.
tips: Measure the liquid exactly.
Add the cheese off the heat, in handfuls.
Loosen with a splash of milk if the sauce tightens.
Grate the cheese yourself for the smoothest sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of milk.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Meatballs
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. Mix with the beef, pork, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley and salt until just combined.
Roll into 16 meatballs, each about the size of a golf ball.
Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Heat the oil and brown the meatballs in 2 batches for 4 minutes each. Remove them.
Pour in the passata and oregano, scraping the base. Add the meatballs on top without stirring.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 15 minutes. Release naturally for 5 minutes and serve.
current_recipe.description: Beef and pork meatballs with parmesan and herbs, browned and then simmered under pressure in tomato sauce for 15 minutes.
tips: Mix the meat gently: overmixing makes it tough.
Do not stir the meatballs into the sauce before cooking.
Wet your hands to stop the mix sticking as you roll.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer in their sauce.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Orange Chicken
ingredients: 600 g chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 3 cm pieces
3 tbsp cornflour, plus 1 tbsp for the sauce
steps: Toss the chicken in 3 tbsp cornflour. Set the Instant Pot to sauté and brown the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger and chilli flakes and stir, scraping the base.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 6 minutes. Release the pressure quickly.
Select sauté. Mix 1 tbsp cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water, stir it in and simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Scatter with the spring onions and sesame seeds and serve.
current_recipe.description: Crisp-coated chicken pieces in a sticky orange sauce made from juice, zest, soy and honey, thickened in the pot after pressure cooking.
tips: Use fresh orange juice and zest for the best flavour.
Thicken only with the lid off.
Reduce the sauce a little longer for a stickier glaze.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of orange juice.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Pulled Pork
ingredients: 1.8 kg boneless pork shoulder, cut into 4 pieces
steps: Mix the sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder and pepper and rub all over the pork.
Set the pot to sauté. Heat the oil and brown the pork for 3 minutes per side. Remove, then add the stock and scrape the base.
Put the onion in the pot and the pork on top. Lock the pressure cooker lid and pressure cook on high for 90 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes.
Shred the pork with two forks, skim the fat from the juices and toss the meat with 120 ml of the juices and the barbecue sauce.
current_recipe.description: A pork shoulder rubbed with spices and pressure cooked until it shreds, then tossed in its own juices and barbecue sauce. Eight servings in 105 minutes.
tips: Cut the shoulder into chunks so it cooks evenly.
Keep the liquid at the base to one cup.
Natural release keeps the meat moist.
Skim the fat from the juices before using them.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days in its juices. Freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat gently, covered.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Risotto
steps: Set the pot to sauté. Melt half the butter with the oil and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble until absorbed. Add the stock and salt and stir once, scraping the base.
Lock the pressure cooker lid and pressure cook on high for 6 minutes. Release the pressure quickly.
Stir vigorously for 1 minute, then add the remaining butter, the parmesan and pepper. Rest for 2 minutes and serve.
current_recipe.description: Arborio rice cooked in stock under pressure with onion and white wine, finished with butter and parmesan. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Toast the rice before adding liquid.
Measure the stock exactly.
Stir hard at the end to bring out the creaminess.
Serve at once; risotto thickens as it stands.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Reheat with a splash of stock if kept for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Salmon
ingredients: 2 salmon fillets, about 300 g, skin on
1 lemon, half sliced and half in wedges
steps: Pour the water into the Instant Pot. Add the lemon slices and dill sprigs and set the trivet on top.
Season the salmon with the salt and pepper. Place the fillets skin side down on the trivet.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 3 minutes. Release the pressure immediately.
Lift the fillets onto plates with a fish slice. Spoon over the melted butter and scatter with the chopped dill.
Serve with the lemon wedges.
current_recipe.description: Salmon fillets steamed over lemon and herbs on a trivet for 3 minutes under pressure, flaking easily and staying moist.
tips: Release the pressure at once to stop the cooking.
Adjust the time for thin or very thick fillets.
Use a fish slice to lift the fillets.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge and is good cold in salads.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Whole Chicken
steps: Mix the paprika, garlic powder, thyme, salt and pepper. Rub it all over the chicken and under the breast skin. Put the lemon halves inside the cavity.
Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Heat the olive oil and brown the chicken breast side down for 5 minutes. Remove it.
Add the stock and onion, set the trivet in the pot and place the chicken on it, breast side up.
Seal and cook on high pressure for 25 minutes. Release naturally for 15 minutes. Check that the thickest part of the thigh reads 74C.
Transfer to a tray and brush with oil. Grill under a hot grill for 5 minutes until the skin is crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before carving.
current_recipe.description: A whole chicken rubbed with paprika and garlic, cooked under pressure for 25 minutes and crisped under the grill for 5.
tips: Weigh the chicken to set the cooking time.
Use a foil sling to lift the bird out whole.
Do not skip the grill: the skin needs it.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Use the carcass for stock.

current_recipe.title: Instant Pot Yogurt
steps: Pour the milk into the Instant Pot. Press the Yogurt button until the display reads Boil, and heat the milk to 82°C.
Cool the milk to 43°C by standing the pot in a sink of cold water, stirring occasionally.
Whisk the live yogurt with a ladleful of the warm milk, then stir it back into the pot.
Set the pot to Yogurt mode for 8 hours without moving it. Stir gently and spoon into jars. Chill before eating.
current_recipe.description: Plain homemade yogurt made from milk and a spoonful of live yogurt, heated and then set in the Instant Pot over eight hours.
tips: Use a thermometer for both temperatures.
Use fresh starter that contains live cultures.
Strain through muslin for thick Greek-style yogurt.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.

current_recipe.title: Irish Cream
ingredients: 2 tsp instant coffee granules dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water
steps: Put the whiskey, condensed milk, cream, chocolate syrup, dissolved coffee, vanilla and almond extract, if using, in a blender.
Blend on low speed for 30 seconds, until smooth and evenly mixed. Do not blend for longer, or the cream may thicken.
Pour into a clean, sealable bottle or jar.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before drinking, so the flavours can blend and the liqueur chills.
Shake well before each use and serve over ice, or stir into coffee.
current_recipe.description: Irish whiskey blended with cream, condensed milk, cocoa, coffee and vanilla into a smooth, sweet liqueur. A homemade version of the shop-bought bottle, made in five minutes.
current_recipe.imageQuery: A glass bottle of creamy pale brown homemade Irish cream liqueur with a small glass of it poured over ice and a dusting of cocoa
tips: Blend for only 30 seconds. The cream can thicken or turn buttery if it is blended for longer.
Shake before serving. The mixture may separate slightly on standing, and a good shake brings it back together at once.
Use a good Irish whiskey. It gives the liqueur its character, and cheap whiskey makes a harsher, less mellow drink.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in a sealed bottle in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. If it smells sour, discard it. Do not freeze.

current_recipe.title: Irish Whiskey Cake
steps: Soak the raisins, sultanas and currants in the tea and 100 ml whiskey overnight. Drain, keeping the liquid.
Heat the oven to 160C and double line a 20 cm tin.
Cream the butter and sugar for 5 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, spice, baking powder and the drained fruit, adding a spoon of liquid if stiff.
Bake for 1 hour until a skewer comes out clean. Prick the warm cake and spoon over 2 tablespoons of whiskey. Cool in the tin and wrap.
current_recipe.description: A rich Irish fruit cake of dried fruit soaked in whiskey and tea, baked slowly for 1 hour and fed with more whiskey.
tips: Soak the fruit overnight.
Double line the tin.
Feed the cake with whiskey weekly.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 6 weeks wrapped, fed with whiskey.

current_recipe.title: Jacket Potato with Cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Scrub the potatoes, prick them with a fork and rub with the oil and salt.
Put them directly on the oven rack and bake for 70 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Cut a cross in the top of each and squeeze open.
Add the butter, then the cheese and pepper, and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: A large potato baked until the skin is crisp and the inside fluffy, split and filled with butter and cheddar.
tips: Do not wrap the potatoes in foil.
Prick the skins before baking.
If your oven runs hot, check at 60 minutes.
Butter first, then cheese.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a hot oven to bring the skin back.

current_recipe.title: Kala Chana
steps: Soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water overnight, for about 8 hours. Drain and rinse.
Put the chickpeas in a pan with 1 litre of fresh water and the salt. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 60 minutes until tender. Drain, keeping the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook for 6 minutes until thick.
Add the chickpeas and 200 ml of their cooking water. Simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few against the pan. Stir in the garam masala, lemon juice and coriander.
current_recipe.description: Dried black chickpeas soaked and simmered until tender, then cooked in a tomato and onion masala with roasted cumin and coriander.
tips: Do not add salt to the soaking water.
Test a chickpea for tenderness before moving on; older ones take longer.
Use a pressure cooker if you have one; it cuts the cooking time by more than half.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Kofte with Yoghurt
ingredients: 1 onion, about 100 g, grated and squeezed
1 clove garlic, crushed, for the yoghurt
steps: Knead the lamb and beef mince with the grated onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, paprika and salt for 1 minute until sticky.
Mould the mixture round eight flat skewers into long sausages.
Grill under a high heat for 12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Stir the garlic into the yoghurt. Warm the flatbreads and spread with the yoghurt, then top with the kofte, tomato and red onion.
current_recipe.description: Spiced lamb and beef kofte shaped round skewers, grilled and served on flatbread with garlic yoghurt and tomato.
tips: Squeeze the onion dry.
Knead until the mince is tacky.
Wet your hands for moulding.
Soak wooden skewers for 20 minutes.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan.

current_recipe.title: Korean Beef Lettuce Wraps
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the mince for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and dry.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and gochujang. Bubble for 2 minutes.
Spoon the beef and rice into the lettuce leaves.
Top with the spring onions, cucumber and sesame seeds.
current_recipe.description: Beef mince fried for 10 minutes with soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic and gochujang, served in crisp lettuce leaves with rice.
tips: Brown the mince until dry.
Do not stir too often.
If your hob runs hot, check at 1 minute.
Use crisp, cup-shaped leaves.
current_recipe.storage: The beef keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Assemble the wraps fresh.

current_recipe.title: Krupnik
ingredients: 300 g smoked bacon or smoked ham hock
steps: Soak the mushrooms in 200 ml of hot water for 20 minutes. Strain, keeping the liquid, and chop the mushrooms.
Simmer the smoked meat in the 2 litres of water for 20 minutes.
Add the barley, carrots, parsnip, celery, leek, bay, mushrooms and their liquid. Simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for 15 minutes more, until the barley is tender.
Remove the bay, shred the meat and return it. Stir in the dill and salt and serve with the soured cream.
current_recipe.description: A thick Polish barley soup with root vegetables and smoked meat or chicken, simmered for 1 hour.
tips: Rinse the barley first.
Add water when reheating, as it thickens.
Use the mushroom liquid for flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Freeze for 3 months.

current_recipe.title: L&P Cake
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C. Grease and line a 20 cm round cake tin.
Beat the butter, sugar and lemon zest for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour alternately with the soft drink until just combined. Spoon into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Mix the icing sugar with the lemon juice and spread over the cooled cake.
current_recipe.description: A light New Zealand cake made with lemon soft drink in the batter, finished with a sharp lemon glaze.
tips: Use the soft drink straight from a freshly opened bottle.
If the top browns too quickly, cover with foil for the last 10 minutes.
Wait until the cake is completely cold before icing, or the glaze runs off.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Lamb Saag
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches for 6 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the onions in the same pan for 8 minutes until deep gold, then add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, garam masala and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, lamb and salt, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the spinach in handfuls, uncover and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
current_recipe.description: Pieces of lamb simmered with spinach, onions, garlic, ginger and spices into a thick green curry.
tips: Brown the lamb in batches.
Cook the onions until deep gold.
Add the spinach in handfuls.
If the sauce is thin, cook it uncovered for longer.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water until hot all the way through.

current_recipe.title: Lamb Shami Kebab
ingredients: 100 g chana dal, soaked for 2 hours and drained
steps: Put the lamb, chana dal, roughly chopped onion, ginger and garlic paste, dried chillies, cumin, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, salt and water in a pan. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the dal is soft.
Uncover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until no liquid remains. Remove the cinnamon stick, cool for 10 minutes, then grind to a smooth, thick paste.
Fold in the chopped onion, green chillies, mint, coriander and egg.
Chill the mixture for 30 minutes, then shape into 12 patties with wet hands.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and cook the patties for 4 minutes on each side, until deep brown and crisp.
current_recipe.description: Soft patties of minced lamb and split chickpeas with whole spices, shaped by hand and shallow-fried until crusty outside.
tips: Test the mixture by rolling a ball; if it cracks, add a spoonful of water.
Handle the patties gently when they are in the pan.
Freeze the shaped, uncooked patties for up to 1 month and fry from frozen.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in a pan with a little oil.

current_recipe.title: Lebanese Cabbage Salad
ingredients: 500 g white cabbage, very finely shredded
steps: Put the cabbage in a large bowl with the salt and rub it with your hands for 1 minute until it softens.
Whisk the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and mint together and pour over the cabbage.
Toss well and leave for 10 minutes.
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed.
current_recipe.description: Finely shredded white cabbage tossed with lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, dried mint and salt.
tips: Slice the cabbage as thin as you can.
Rub the salt in to soften the leaves.
Leave the salad to stand before serving.
Use a single clove of garlic, since it is raw.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days, getting softer and sharper as it stands.

current_recipe.title: Leg of Lamb
ingredients: 2.2 kg leg of lamb, bone in
4 sprigs rosemary, plus 2 extra for the tin
steps: Take the lamb out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Heat the oven to 220C.
Cut about 20 small slits into the lamb. Push a garlic sliver and a rosemary sprig into each. Rub with the oil, salt and pepper.
Set the lamb on the sliced onion in a roasting tin. Roast for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven to 170C and roast for 1 hour 25 minutes more, until a thermometer reads 57C for pink.
Transfer the lamb to a board, cover with foil and rest for 20 minutes.
Pour the wine into the tin, scrape the base and boil for 5 minutes. Add the stock, simmer for 5 minutes, strain and serve with the carved lamb.
current_recipe.description: A bone-in leg of lamb studded with garlic and rosemary and roasted for 1 hour 45 minutes, then rested until pink and tender.
tips: Use a thermometer for the right doneness.
Rest the lamb for at least 20 minutes.
Carve across the grain.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Slice thinly for sandwiches.

current_recipe.title: Lemon Blueberry Cake
steps: Heat the oven to 175C. Grease and line two 20 cm round tins.
Rub the lemon zest into the caster sugar. Beat with the 225 g butter for 4 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt in 3 additions, alternating with the buttermilk. Fold in the blueberries.
Divide between the tins and bake for 35 minutes. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, 100 g butter, icing sugar and lemon juice until smooth. Sandwich the layers and cover the cake.
current_recipe.description: A two-layer lemon sponge with fresh blueberries in the batter and a lemon cream cheese frosting, baked for 35 minutes.
tips: Weigh the batter into the tins for even layers.
Cool the cakes completely before frosting.
Chill the cake briefly to set the frosting.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

current_recipe.title: Lemon Chicken Orzo
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Season the chicken with the oregano, half the salt and the pepper.
Toast the orzo in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 2 minutes. Stir in the stock, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt.
Lay the chicken skin-side up on top and bake uncovered for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the orzo has absorbed the stock.
Stir the spinach into the orzo, rest for 5 minutes and serve.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs and orzo baked together in a lemon, garlic and oregano stock until the pasta has soaked up the juices.
tips: Toast the orzo first.
Keep the skin above the liquid.
If your oven runs hot, check at 25 minutes.
Add the spinach at the end.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water, as the orzo thickens.

current_recipe.title: Lemon Drizzle Loaf
steps: Heat the oven to 175C. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoonful of the flour each time.
Fold in the remaining flour, lemon zest and milk. Spoon into the tin.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Prick the hot cake all over with a skewer. Mix the granulated sugar with the lemon juice and spoon over slowly. Cool completely in the tin.
current_recipe.description: A classic British lemon loaf soaked while warm in lemon and sugar syrup, which sets into a crisp, sugary crust.
tips: Pour the syrup over while the cake is hot.
Prick the cake all over first.
Leave the sugar crystals undissolved.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Lemon Gelato
steps: Heat the milk, cream and lemon zest until steaming. Cover and infuse for 20 minutes, then remove the zest.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and salt until pale. Reheat the milk, whisk a ladle into the yolks and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat to 80C, stirring, then strain and chill for 4 hours.
Stir the lemon juice into the cold custard and taste. Churn until thick and glossy.
Freeze in a covered container for 3 hours.
current_recipe.description: An Italian-style gelato made with milk, a little cream and fresh lemon, chilled for 4 hours, churned and frozen for 3 hours.
tips: Avoid the white pith when peeling the zest.
Add the lemon juice to the cold custard.
Soften for 5 minutes before serving.
current_recipe.storage: Best within 3 days. Keeps in the freezer for 1 week.

current_recipe.title: Maids of Honour
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and grease a 12-hole tart tin. Cut 12 rounds from the pastry and press them into the tin.
Put half a teaspoon of jam in each case.
Beat the ricotta with the ground almonds, caster sugar, egg and lemon zest. Spoon into the cases to two-thirds full.
Bake for 25 minutes until risen and deep gold. Cool for 5 minutes and dust with the icing sugar.
current_recipe.description: Small puff pastry tarts with a spoonful of raspberry jam and a lemony ricotta and almond filling.
tips: Drain the ricotta.
Do not overfill the cases.
If your oven runs hot, check at 20 minutes.
Eat the same day.
current_recipe.storage: Best on the day. Keeps in an airtight tin for 2 days.

current_recipe.title: Meal Prep Chicken and Rice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Rub the chicken with the oil, paprika, garlic and salt and roast on a tray for 20 minutes, until cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes.
Boil the rice for 12 minutes, drain and spread on a tray to cool.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes.
Slice the chicken and divide the rice, chicken and broccoli among four boxes. Drizzle with the soy sauce when you eat.
current_recipe.description: Chicken breast roasted with paprika and garlic, packed with rice and broccoli into four boxes for the week. Four servings in 45 minutes.
tips: Do not overcook the chicken.
Cool the rice quickly.
If your oven runs hot, check the chicken at 15 minutes.
Reheat only once, until piping hot.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days in sealed boxes. Reheat once, until steaming hot.

current_recipe.title: Mejillones a la Marinera
steps: Scrub the mussels and pull off the beards. Discard any open ones that do not close when tapped.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes. Add the paprika, tomato sauce and wine and boil for 1 minute.
Add the mussels, cover at once and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan.
Discard any that stay shut. Add the parsley and serve with the lemon and bread.
current_recipe.description: Mussels steamed open in white wine with garlic, tomato, paprika and parsley, a Spanish bar classic ready in 20 minutes.
tips: Take the mussels off the heat as soon as they open.
Cover the pan at once.
Throw away any that stay shut.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh.

current_recipe.title: Membrillo
ingredients: 1 kg quinces, peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Put the quinces and water in a pan, bring to a boil and simmer for 30 minutes until very soft.
Purée until smooth, then return to the pan with the sugar and lemon juice.
Cook over low heat for 90 minutes, stirring often, until the paste is very thick and deep red.
Pour into a lined 20 cm square tin and smooth the top. Leave to set for 8 hours, then turn out and slice.
current_recipe.description: A firm, ruby-coloured Spanish paste of quince and sugar, cooked slowly, set in a tin and served with cheese.
tips: Wear oven gloves; the hot paste spits.
Stir from the bottom as the paste thickens.
Wrap the set paste in baking paper and keep it cool.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps wrapped in the fridge for 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Menestra de Verduras
ingredients: 200 g green asparagus, in 4 cm lengths
steps: Trim the artichokes, quarter them and rub with the lemon juice.
Soften the onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the wine and stock.
Add the artichokes and carrots and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the broad beans and asparagus for 8 minutes, then the peas for 4 minutes.
Fry the ham in the remaining oil until crisp.
Season the stew with the salt and serve topped with the ham.
current_recipe.description: A Navarra stew of artichokes, peas, broad beans, asparagus and ham in a light sauce, ready in 55 minutes.
tips: Add the vegetables in order of cooking time.
Keep them green by not overcooking.
Use good frozen vegetables if the fresh ones are not in season.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Microwave Rice Pudding
steps: Put the rice, milk, sugar and butter in a large microwave-safe bowl and stir.
Microwave on medium power for 5 minutes. Stir well, scraping the base.
Microwave for 5 minutes more on medium and stir again. Repeat for a final 5 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla and leave for 5 minutes to thicken.
Serve with a grating of nutmeg and the jam.
current_recipe.description: Pudding rice, milk, sugar and nutmeg cooked in the microwave in stages for 15 minutes into a creamy, spoonable rice pudding.
tips: Use a very large bowl.
Stir every 5 minutes.
Leave to rest: the pudding thickens as it cools.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Stir in a splash of milk when reheating.

current_recipe.title: Mint Jelly
steps: Put the apple juice and jam sugar in a large pan and stir over medium heat until the sugar has dissolved.
Bring to a full rolling boil and boil for 5 minutes, skimming off any foam.
Take off the heat and stir in the vinegar and mint. Leave for 5 minutes.
Stir and pour into clean, warm jars. Cool until set.
current_recipe.description: A clear, green-flecked jelly of apple juice, vinegar and mint, set with jam sugar and served with roast lamb.
tips: Use clear apple juice.
Keep a full rolling boil.
If your hob runs hot, stir often.
Keep it in the fridge.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks. This is a fridge jelly, not a canning recipe.

current_recipe.title: Miso Dressing
steps: Whisk the miso, rice vinegar and warm water until completely smooth.
Add the honey and ginger and whisk again.
Whisk in the vegetable oil and sesame oil, then the lime juice. Taste and adjust.
current_recipe.description: A savoury, slightly sweet dressing of white miso, rice vinegar, sesame oil and ginger whisked until smooth.
tips: Warm the water slightly to dissolve the miso more quickly.
Add more water for a thinner dressing.
Use a jar and shake if you do not want to whisk.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week. Whisk or shake before using.

current_recipe.title: Mole Verde
ingredients: 1 large bunch fresh coriander, about 60 g
8 chicken thighs on the bone, poached, about 1 kg
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they swell and pop. Cool, then grind to a fine powder.
Boil the tomatillos, chillies, onion and garlic in water for 8 minutes. Drain and blend with the coriander, parsley, lettuce, ground seeds and 250 ml of the stock until smooth.
Heat the lard in a wide pot and fry the sauce for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Add the remaining stock, salt and the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.
current_recipe.description: Chicken simmered in a thick green sauce of pumpkin seeds, tomatillos, green chillies and fresh herbs, a lighter cousin of mole poblano.
tips: Stir the sauce constantly while it fries.
Do not overcook the herbs.
Add water if the sauce is too thick.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. The colour dulls but the taste holds.

current_recipe.title: Moroccan Orange Salad
steps: Cut the peel and pith from the oranges. Slice into thin rounds, discarding any pips.
Overlap the slices on a wide plate. Pour over any juice and the orange blossom water.
Dust with the icing sugar and cinnamon. Chill for 30 minutes.
Scatter with the mint and olives, if using, before serving.
current_recipe.description: Sliced oranges with cinnamon, orange blossom water, mint and black olives, served chilled as a refreshing salad or dessert.
tips: Use a sharp knife to cut away every trace of pith.
Add the cinnamon just before serving.
A handful of pomegranate seeds makes it look festive.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten within 2 hours of slicing. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Mushroom Burgers
steps: Wipe the mushrooms and mix the oil, vinegar, garlic and thyme. Brush the mushrooms with it and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat the grill to medium-high. Grill the mushrooms gills-up for 7 minutes, then turn and grill for 8 minutes more.
Lay a slice of cheddar on each for the last minute.
Toast the buns and fill with rocket, tomato and a mushroom.
current_recipe.description: Large field mushrooms marinated in balsamic, garlic and thyme, grilled for 15 minutes and served in buns with cheese. Four servings in 25 minutes.
tips: Wipe the mushrooms rather than washing them.
Start gills-up.
If your grill runs hot, check at 10 minutes.
Salt after cooking if you can.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Cooked mushrooms keep in the fridge for 2 days.

current_recipe.title: Nasi Uduk
steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, galangal, bay leaves and salt in a pan. Bring to a boil, stir once, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes without lifting the lid. Remove the aromatics and fluff with a fork.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the eggs sunny-side up.
Serve the rice topped with the egg, shallots, sambal and cucumber.
current_recipe.description: Coconut rice cooked with lemongrass, galangal and bay leaves, a Jakarta breakfast served with fried shallots, egg and sambal.
tips: Use full-fat coconut milk.
Keep the heat low once covered.
Add fried anchovies for a traditional touch.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: No Bake Chocolate Pie
ingredients: 150 ml double cream, whipped, to top
steps: Mix the biscuit crumbs and melted butter and press firmly into a 23 cm pie dish. Chill for 15 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, cocoa, cornflour and salt in a pan. Whisk in the milk and 200 ml cream gradually and bring to a simmer, whisking, for 5 minutes until thick.
Whisk a ladle of the hot filling into the egg yolks, then whisk it all back into the pan for 1 minute. Off the heat, stir in the chocolate and vanilla until smooth.
Strain into the crust and press cling film onto the surface. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Top with the whipped cream.
current_recipe.description: A silky chocolate pudding pie in a crushed biscuit crust, made on the hob in 5 minutes and chilled for 4 hours.
tips: Whisk the cornflour with the dry ingredients first.
Strain the filling for a smooth top.
Cover the surface with cling film while it cools.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: No Bake Key Lime Pie
ingredients: 300 ml double cream, whipped to soft peaks
100 ml double cream, whipped, to serve
steps: Mix the biscuit crumbs and melted butter and press into a 23 cm pie dish. Chill for 15 minutes.
Stir the condensed milk with the lime juice and zest slowly until thickened.
Fold in the 300 ml whipped cream in 2 additions.
Pour into the crust and smooth the top.
Chill for at least 4 hours and top with the remaining whipped cream.
current_recipe.description: Lime juice, condensed milk and whipped cream in a graham cracker crust, chilled for 4 hours to a cool, tangy set.
tips: Use fresh lime juice, not bottled.
Fold in the cream gently.
Chill for at least 4 hours.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: No Churn Ice Cream
steps: Chill a large bowl and whisk in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks.
Fold in the condensed milk in 2 additions, then the vanilla and salt, until just combined.
Pour into a lined 900 g loaf tin and press greaseproof paper over the surface.
Freeze for at least 6 hours. Stand at room temperature for 10 minutes before scooping.
current_recipe.description: Whipped double cream folded with sweetened condensed milk and vanilla, frozen for 6 hours into a scoopable ice cream with no machine.
tips: Whip the cream to stiff peaks.
Fold gently to keep the air in.
Cover the surface to stop ice crystals.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the freezer for 2 weeks.

current_recipe.title: Nougat de Montelimar
steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with rice paper. Warm the almonds and pistachios in a 150C oven for 10 minutes.
Warm the honey in a heavy pan to 125C. In another pan, boil the sugar and water to 145C.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks. With the mixer running, pour in the honey in a thin stream, then the sugar syrup, whisking for 8 minutes until thick and glossy.
Fold in the warm nuts and vanilla with an oiled spatula.
Press into the tin, cover with rice paper and weigh down. Leave overnight to set.
Cut into 24 pieces with an oiled knife.
current_recipe.description: A soft white nougat of honey, sugar, whisked egg white, almonds and pistachios, cooked to hard ball stage and set overnight.
tips: Use a thermometer; the temperature decides the texture.
Pour the hot syrup in a thin stream with the mixer running.
Oil the knife to cut cleanly.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 weeks wrapped in paper in an airtight tin.

current_recipe.title: Oatmeal Bars
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the bananas, peanut butter, honey and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in the oats, cinnamon, salt and raisins. Press firmly into the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool for 15 minutes in the tin, then cut into 9 squares.
current_recipe.description: Rolled oats, banana, peanut butter and honey baked into soft bars for grab-and-go breakfasts. Makes nine in 50 minutes.
tips: Use very ripe bananas for the best sweetness.
Press the mix down firmly so the bars hold together.
Check for peanut allergies before sharing.
current_recipe.storage: Keep in an airtight tin in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freezes for up to 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Olan
ingredients: 400 g ash gourd or courgette, peeled and cut into 3 cm pieces
200 ml thin coconut milk (coconut milk diluted with 100 ml water)
steps: Put the gourd, chillies, water and salt in a pan. Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until just tender.
Add the black-eyed beans and thin coconut milk and warm through gently for 3 minutes.
Lower the heat and stir in the thick coconut milk. Warm for 2 minutes without letting it boil.
Off the heat, stir in the coconut oil and curry leaves.
current_recipe.description: A pale, mild Kerala stew of ash gourd and black-eyed beans simmered in coconut milk, seasoned with green chilli and finished with coconut oil.
tips: Do not let the coconut milk boil.
Slit the chillies rather than chop them for a mild heat.
Taste for salt before the coconut oil goes in.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Black Bean Soup
ingredients: 720 g tinned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot. Cook the onion, pepper and celery for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans, stock, bay leaf and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Blend about a third of the soup with a stick blender, leaving the rest chunky.
Stir in the lime juice and vinegar and taste for seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and top with the soured cream and coriander.
current_recipe.description: Black beans, onion, peppers and cumin simmered in a single pot for 40 minutes, then partly blended for a thick, smoky soup.
tips: Blend only part of the soup for body and texture.
Add the acid at the end.
Thin with stock if it thickens on standing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Breakfast
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Cook the bacon in a large lidded pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp. Lift out, leaving 2 tbsp of fat in the pan.
Add the potatoes, salt and paprika, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once.
Uncover, add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes until the potatoes are golden.
Make 4 wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with the bacon, cheddar and chives and serve from the pan.
current_recipe.description: Bacon, potatoes, onion and eggs cooked in a single pan in 20 minutes, finished with cheese and chives.
tips: Use the bacon fat to cook the potatoes.
Cover the pan to set the egg whites.
Cut the potatoes evenly.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. The potato mix keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Garlic Parmesan Chicken
ingredients: 700 g chicken thighs, boneless and skinless
steps: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a deep pan with a lid over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side and remove it.
Cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and orzo and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, scraping the base. Return the chicken and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 12 minutes, stirring once, until the orzo is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the parmesan, cream and lemon zest. Scatter with parsley and serve.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs browned in a single pan, then simmered with orzo, stock, garlic and parmesan until the pasta absorbs the sauce.
tips: Toast the orzo briefly for flavour.
Stir once only during cooking.
Add the parmesan off the heat for a smooth sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Add a splash of stock when reheating.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Gnocchi
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes, pressing them with a spoon as they burst.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Add the gnocchi and cook for 7 minutes, stirring gently, until plump and tender.
Take off the heat. Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the cream, parmesan and salt.
Scatter with the basil and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Shop-bought gnocchi simmered in the pan with spinach, cherry tomatoes, garlic and cream until the sauce coats each dumpling.
tips: Cook the gnocchi straight from the packet.
Press the tomatoes to release their juice.
Add the cream and spinach off the heat.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Keeps for 1 day in the fridge but the gnocchi soften.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Lasagne Soup
steps: In one large pot, brown the mince and onion for 10 minutes until dry. Add the garlic, tomato puree and herbs for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes and stock and bring to the boil.
Add the broken lasagne sheets and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often. Stir in the spinach and salt for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with the ricotta, mozzarella and parmesan.
current_recipe.description: Beef mince, tomatoes, stock and broken lasagne sheets simmered in one pot for 30 minutes and finished with ricotta.
tips: Brown the mince thoroughly.
Stir often so the pasta does not stick.
If your hob runs hot, check at 12 minutes.
Add the cheese at the table.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. The pasta softens, so add a splash of stock when reheating.

current_recipe.title: One Pot Ramen
steps: Bring the stock, garlic, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a large pot. Cook for 10 minutes.
Whisk in the miso paste. Add the noodles and cook for 3 minutes, separating them with a fork.
Add the pak choi and cook for 2 minutes. Crack the eggs into the simmering broth and poach for 3 minutes.
Ladle into 2 deep bowls, lifting the eggs on top.
Finish with the spring onions, sesame oil and chilli flakes.
current_recipe.description: Ramen noodles, soy broth, a soft egg and spring onions cooked in a single pan in 15 minutes, with a splash of sesame oil to finish.
tips: Add the miso at the end so it does not turn bitter.
Do not overcook the noodles.
Taste the broth: it should be slightly salty.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. The noodles soften if stored.

current_recipe.title: Painkiller
ingredients: 1 orange wedge and 1 pineapple leaf, to garnish
steps: Put the rum, pineapple juice, orange juice and coconut cream in a cocktail shaker with a handful of ice and shake hard for 15 seconds, until the outside is frosted and the drink is frothy.
Strain into a tall glass filled with crushed ice.
Grate fresh nutmeg generously over the top.
Garnish with the orange wedge and pineapple leaf and serve with a straw.
current_recipe.description: Dark rum shaken with pineapple juice, orange juice and sweet coconut cream, served over crushed ice with fresh nutmeg on top. The tropical drink of the British Virgin Islands.
current_recipe.imageQuery: A tall glass of creamy golden Painkiller cocktail over crushed ice, dusted with fresh nutmeg, with an orange wedge and pineapple leaf
tips: Shake it hard. The coconut cream and pineapple juice make a foam when shaken, and a long shake gives the drink its creamy top.
Grate the nutmeg fresh. It is part of the drink, and pre-ground nutmeg has lost most of its aroma.
Choose a dark or navy-style rum. It has a richer, more caramel flavour than white rum and stands up to the fruit.
current_recipe.storage: Best made and drunk at once. The juices and rum can be combined ahead and kept in the fridge for a day, with the coconut cream added and shaken when serving.

current_recipe.title: Pannenkoeken
steps: Whisk the flour, milk, eggs and salt to a smooth batter. Stand for 15 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a 26 cm pan over medium high heat. Lay 2 rashers of bacon in the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in a quarter of the batter to cover the pan in a thin layer. Cook for 2 minutes until the underside is golden, then flip and cook for 1 minute.
Repeat for the remaining pancakes, topping some with apple slices. Keep warm in a low oven.
Serve with the syrup and icing sugar.
current_recipe.description: Large, thin Dutch pancakes fried in butter and eaten with syrup, bacon or apple, ready in 45 minutes.
tips: Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Use a large non stick pan.
Add toppings before flipping.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat in a pan.

current_recipe.title: Pasta alla Norcina
ingredients: 400 g short pasta such as penne
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat from the skins and fry it in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the shallot and cook for 2 minutes, then add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Pour in the cream and simmer for 2 minutes.
Boil the pasta in salted water until tender. Keep 100 ml of the water, then drain.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the water, pecorino and pepper.
current_recipe.description: Pasta in a sauce of crumbled pork sausage, cream and pecorino, named for Norcia and ready in 30 minutes.
tips: Break up the sausage so it browns well.
Keep a little of the fat for flavour.
Loosen the sauce with pasta water.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Pasta con le Zucchine
ingredients: 400 g short pasta, such as penne
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the courgettes with the garlic and half the salt for 12 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges.
Boil the pasta in salted water until tender. Keep 200 ml of the water, then drain.
Add the pasta to the courgettes with 100 ml of the water and crush some of the courgettes with a spoon.
Off the heat add the Parmesan, basil, lemon zest and pepper and toss, adding water to loosen.
current_recipe.description: Short pasta tossed with sweet softened courgettes, garlic, basil and Parmesan, ready in 30 minutes.
tips: Let the courgettes colour before stirring.
Crush some pieces to make a sauce.
Add the cheese off the heat.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Peanut Butter Smoothie
steps: Pour the milk into a blender, then add the peanut butter, honey and bananas in pieces.
Add the ice on top and blend on high for 45 seconds until smooth.
Pour into two glasses and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: A thick smoothie of banana, peanut butter, milk and honey, blended with ice until smooth.
tips: Add the ice last.
Freeze the banana for a thicker drink.
If it is too thick, add a splash of milk.
Serve at once.
current_recipe.storage: Best drunk at once. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day; stir before drinking.

current_recipe.title: Pear Cake
steps: Heat the oven to 175C. Grease and line a 23 cm springform tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, ground almonds, baking powder and salt with the milk. Spread in the tin.
Peel, core and slice the pears and toss with the lemon juice. Fan the slices over the batter and press them in halfway.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 15 minutes and dust with the icing sugar.
current_recipe.description: A French-style cake with ground almonds and sliced pears set into the batter, baked for 50 minutes and served warm.
tips: Use ripe but firm pears.
Toss the slices in lemon juice.
Press the fruit halfway into the batter.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Pita Chips
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Split each pita into two rounds and cut each into 8 triangles.
Toss in a bowl with the oil, za'atar and salt, and spread in one layer on two trays.
Cook for 10 minutes, turning once, until golden. Cool on a rack.
current_recipe.description: Pita breads cut into triangles, tossed in olive oil, za'atar and salt and cooked for 10 minutes until crisp. Four servings in 15 minutes.
tips: Split the pitas into two layers.
Spread them in a single layer.
If your oven runs hot, check at 7 minutes.
Judge crispness once cool.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Pizza Bread
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Lay the bread on two trays and bake for 3 minutes.
Mix the purée, water, oregano and salt. Spread thinly over the bread, right to the edges.
Cover with the mozzarella and drizzle with the oil.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and spotted brown.
current_recipe.description: Sliced bread spread with tomato purée and oregano, covered in mozzarella and baked until the edges crisp. Four servings in 17 minutes.
tips: Toast the bread first for a crisp base.
Spread the sauce thin.
Watch the last 2 minutes; the cheese browns quickly.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day; reheat at 200°C for 5 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Placinta cu Branza
steps: Mix the flour, 5 tablespoons of oil, water and salt and knead for 5 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190C. Mix the cheese, eggs, soured cream, dill and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin into a rectangle. Spread the filling along one long side and roll up.
Coil the roll into a spiral on a lined tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep gold. Cut into squares.
current_recipe.description: A Romanian cheese pie of thin pastry filled with salty cheese, egg and dill and baked until crisp, in 1 hour 15 minutes.
tips: Taste the filling before adding salt.
Roll the dough very thin.
Serve warm or cold.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in the oven.

current_recipe.title: Po Boy Sandwich
ingredients: 60 ml vegetable oil, for shallow frying
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, hot sauce and pickles into a remoulade.
Toss the prawns in the buttermilk, then the flour, then the cornmeal mixed with the Cajun seasoning.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan until a crumb sizzles at once and fry the prawns in batches for 2 minutes a side until deep gold. Drain on kitchen paper.
Split and lightly toast the rolls, spread with the remoulade and fill with the lettuce, tomato and prawns. Serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Cornmeal-fried prawns piled into a crusty roll with lettuce, tomato, pickles and remoulade.
tips: Keep the oil hot enough to sizzle.
Fry in small batches.
Drain on kitchen paper.
Fill the rolls at the last moment.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep the remoulade in the fridge for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Polpettone
ingredients: 2 slices white bread, 60 g, soaked in 100 ml milk
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Squeeze the bread and mash it into the beef, pork, mortadella, eggs, Parmesan, parsley, garlic and salt. Mix lightly.
Shape into a log 25 cm long.
Spread half the passata in a baking dish, set the loaf on it and pour over the rest.
Bake for 60 minutes, spooning the sauce over the loaf twice, until firm.
Rest for 10 minutes and slice.
current_recipe.description: An Italian meatloaf of beef and pork with mortadella, Parmesan and parsley, baked for 60 minutes in tomato sauce.
tips: Do not overmix the meat.
Squeeze the soaked bread before mixing.
Rest before slicing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Freeze sliced for 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Pommes Anna
steps: Heat the oven to 200C. Slice the potatoes 2 mm thick on a mandoline and pat dry in a cloth without washing.
Brush a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan with butter. Arrange a circle of overlapping slices in the base, brush with butter and season lightly.
Repeat the layers, brushing each with butter and seasoning, until all the potatoes are used. Press down firmly.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until the base sizzles. Cover with buttered paper and put in the oven.
Bake for 40 minutes, pressing down after 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the base golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate.
current_recipe.description: Thin potato slices layered with melted butter in a pan, baked until the base is golden and crisp, then turned out like a cake, 50 minutes.
tips: Slice thinly and evenly, and do not rinse the potato.
Use skimmed, melted butter so the layers brown without burning.
Press the cake down once during baking.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Crisp in a hot oven for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Pommes Dauphine
ingredients: 60 ml rapeseed oil absorbed, from 750 ml for frying
steps: Bake the potatoes at 200C for 50 minutes until soft. Scoop out the flesh and pass it through a ricer. Leave to steam for 10 minutes.
Heat the water and butter in a pan until the butter melts and the water boils. Tip in the flour and beat to a smooth paste that leaves the sides of the pan.
Beat in the egg and the yolk, a little at a time, until glossy.
Fold the choux into the potato with the nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oil to 170C. Drop in heaped teaspoonfuls, five or six at a time, and fry for 4 minutes until puffed and golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Light, crisp potato croquettes made by folding mashed potato into choux pastry, shaped into balls and deep fried for about 20 minutes.
tips: Keep the potato dry by baking it rather than boiling.
Fry in small batches so the oil stays at 170C.
Serve straight away; they soften as they cool.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Re-crisp in a 200C oven for 8 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Prego no Pao
ingredients: 500 g thin beef sirloin steaks, 5 mm
steps: Beat the steaks to 5 mm. Mix the wine, garlic, bay and salt and marinate the steaks for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan until very hot. Fry the steaks for 1 minute on each side, in batches. Lift out.
Add the butter and 4 tablespoons of the marinade to the pan and bubble for 2 minutes.
Split the rolls, dip the cut sides in the sauce, spread with mustard and fill with the steak.
current_recipe.description: A thin steak marinated in garlic and wine, fried briefly and served in a crusty roll with its juices, ready in 25 minutes.
tips: Beat the steak thin.
Fry for one minute a side, no more.
Dip the roll in the pan juices.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh.

current_recipe.title: Puerto Rican Tembleque
steps: Mix the cornflour with 100 ml of the coconut milk until smooth.
Heat the remaining coconut milk with the sugar and salt until steaming. Pour in the cornflour mixture and stir constantly over a medium heat for 8 minutes until very thick.
Pour into a lightly oiled 1-litre mould or 8 ramekins and cool for 20 minutes, then chill for at least 3 hours.
Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a plate and dust with the cinnamon and coconut flakes.
current_recipe.description: A wobbly white pudding of coconut milk set with cornflour, topped with ground cinnamon, a Puerto Rican Christmas dessert.
tips: Stir constantly while it thickens.
Oil the mould lightly.
Serve cold.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Pumpkin Hummus
steps: Whip the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute until pale and creamy.
Add the chickpeas, pumpkin puree, garlic, cumin, paprika and salt and blend for 3 minutes, scraping down.
With the machine running, add the oil gradually. Taste and adjust.
Spoon into a bowl and dust with a little paprika.
current_recipe.description: Hummus blended with plain pumpkin puree, tahini, smoked paprika and cumin into a creamy orange dip.
tips: Use plain pumpkin puree.
Blot the puree if wet.
Whip the tahini first.
Taste and add lemon.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.

current_recipe.title: Rajska Omacka
steps: Simmer the beef with the bay in the water for 1 hour 30 minutes. Lift out and keep the broth.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 3 minutes, then the purée and sugar.
Whisk in 700 ml of the broth a ladle at a time. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, cream and salt.
Slice the beef and serve with the dumplings and sauce.
current_recipe.description: A sweet Czech tomato sauce with beef and bread dumplings, the beef simmered for an hour and a half, a classic school dinner.
tips: Cook the roux before adding the broth.
Balance the sweetness with vinegar.
Slice the beef against the grain.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Ranch Water
ingredients: 120 ml very cold sparkling mineral water
Fine salt, for the rim, optional
steps: Run a lime wedge round the rim of a tall glass and dip it in fine salt, if you like a salted rim.
Fill the glass with ice. Pour in the tequila and lime juice.
Top up with the sparkling mineral water and stir once, gently, to keep the bubbles.
Garnish with the lime wedge and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Blanco tequila, fresh lime juice and sparkling mineral water over ice in a tall, salt-rimmed glass. The crisp, dry, low-sugar West Texas highball.
current_recipe.imageQuery: A tall ranch water cocktail in a salt-rimmed glass with ice, lime wedges and bubbles, on a wooden table in bright West Texas light
tips: Use a blanco tequila made from 100 per cent agave. Cheap mixed tequilas have a harsh, sweet taste that the lime cannot cover.
Squeeze the lime juice fresh, just before mixing. Bottled juice is flat and slightly bitter.

Keep the sparkling water in the fridge until the last second and stir only once. The drink is only as good as its bubbles, and a mineral water with plenty of dissolved minerals adds a faint saltiness that suits the tequila and the lime.
current_recipe.storage: Best made to order. Once the sparkling water is added, it goes flat in minutes, so build the drink in the glass and drink it while it is cold and fizzy.

current_recipe.title: Ratatouille Bake
ingredients: 300 g aubergine, cut into 2 cm chunks
300 g courgette, cut into 2 cm chunks
200 g red pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks
1 onion, about 150 g, cut into wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Toss the aubergine, courgette, pepper, onion and garlic with the oil, thyme, salt and pepper.
Spread them in a wide, shallow baking dish.
Pour over the passata and tomatoes and stir lightly.
Bake for 50 minutes, stirring once at 25 minutes, until soft and thickened. Rest for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Aubergine, courgette, peppers and tomatoes baked in one dish with garlic, thyme and olive oil until soft and sweet.
tips: Use a wide, shallow dish.
Cut the vegetables the same size.
If your oven runs hot, check at 40 minutes.
Stir once halfway.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. It tastes better the next day.

current_recipe.title: Raw Mango Curry
ingredients: 2 raw green mangoes, about 500 g, peeled and cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Put the mango, turmeric, salt and water in a pan. Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the mango is just soft.
Grind the coconut, green chillies and cumin to a coarse paste with 2 tablespoons of water.
Stir the paste into the mango with the jaggery and simmer for 3 minutes. Lower the heat, add the yoghurt and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds, dried chilli and curry leaves until they crackle, and pour over the curry.
current_recipe.description: Sour green mango simmered in a mild coconut, yoghurt and turmeric sauce, finished with a tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves.
tips: Taste a piece of mango before cooking to judge how sour it is.
Add the jaggery gradually.
Do not boil once the yoghurt is in.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently.

current_recipe.title: Red Lentil Kofte
steps: Simmer the lentils in the water for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and thick.
Stir in the bulgur, take the pan off the heat, cover and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil, cook the onion for 5 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, cumin and chilli flakes and add to the lentils with the salt and lemon juice.
Cool until you can handle it. Mix in the spring onions and parsley and shape into small ovals with damp hands. Serve on lettuce leaves.
current_recipe.description: Turkish red lentil and bulgur balls with spring onion, tomato paste and cumin, shaped by hand and served cold in lettuce.
tips: Add the bulgur off the heat.
Season boldly, as the flavour mellows as it cools.
Wet your hands to shape the kofte.
Serve with plenty of lemon.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Serve cold.

current_recipe.title: Rhabarberkuchen
ingredients: 100 g caster sugar, for the meringue
steps: Heat the oven to 170C and line a 24 x 30 cm tin. Toss the rhubarb with 1 tablespoon of the caster sugar.
Beat the butter and 200 g sugar until pale. Beat in the 4 yolks and the vanilla, then fold in the flour and baking powder.
Spread in the tin and press the rhubarb on top. Bake for 25 minutes.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, whisk in the 100 g sugar a spoonful at a time and spread over the cake.
Bake for 20 minutes more until pale gold. Cool in the tin and dust with the icing sugar.
current_recipe.description: A tray bake of buttery sponge topped with rhubarb and a soft meringue, baked for 45 minutes and cut in squares.
tips: Bake the base before adding the meringue.
Cut the rhubarb into even pieces.
Cool completely before cutting.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in a tin.

current_recipe.title: Risotto agli Asparagi
steps: Cut off the asparagus tips 4 cm from the top. Chop the stalks small. Simmer the tough ends in the water with the salt for 15 minutes, then strain and keep hot.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes. Add the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes, adding the chopped stalks after 8 minutes and the tips for the last 4 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Creamy risotto with asparagus tips stirred in at the end and a stock made from the trimmed stalks, ready in 40 minutes.
tips: Simmer the woody ends for stock, not the bin.
Add the tips at the end to keep them green.
Beat in cold butter off the heat.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Risotto al Radicchio
steps: Melt half the butter in a wide pan and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add half the radicchio and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Stir in the rest of the radicchio for the last 3 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan. Rest for 2 minutes and season with the pepper.
current_recipe.description: Creamy risotto with red radicchio softened in butter and red wine, finished with Parmesan, in 40 minutes.
tips: Add the second half of the radicchio at the end.
Keep the stock hot.
Beat in cold butter off the heat for a glossy finish.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Reheat with a splash of stock.

current_recipe.title: Risotto allo Zafferano
ingredients: 1.2 litres chicken or vegetable stock, hot
steps: Steep the saffron in 100 ml of the hot stock for 10 minutes.
Melt half the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed. Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes, adding the saffron stock for the last 5 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Taste for salt and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Creamy risotto coloured and scented with saffron, finished with butter and Parmesan, in 40 minutes.
tips: Steep the saffron before you begin.
Add the saffron late to keep its scent.
Beat in cold butter off the heat.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. Leftovers can be fried into rice cakes.

current_recipe.title: Roast Cabbage Wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and put a large tray inside to heat.
Cut the cabbage into 8 wedges, leaving the core in each. Brush all over with the oil and sprinkle with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Lay the wedges cut-side down on the hot tray and roast for 15 minutes. Turn and roast for 15 minutes more until the edges are dark and the middle is tender.
Squeeze over the lemon juice before serving.
current_recipe.description: Thick wedges of white cabbage brushed with oil and roasted until the edges char and the centre turns sweet and tender.
tips: Keep the core in so the wedges hold together.
Preheat the tray for better browning.
Check the wedges at 25 minutes if your oven runs hot.
Serve with a dollop of yoghurt or mustard mayonnaise.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven.

current_recipe.title: Roasted Potatoes and Onions
ingredients: 1.2 kg floury potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large roasting tray inside. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, drain and shake in the colander to roughen the edges.
Pour the oil onto the hot tray and add the potatoes, turning to coat. Roast for 20 minutes.
Turn the potatoes and add the onions. Roast for 25 minutes more, turning once, until deep golden.
Sprinkle with the thyme and salt and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Potato chunks and onion wedges roasted at a high heat with oil and thyme until crisp and golden. Four servings in 55 minutes.
tips: Shake the parboiled potatoes to roughen the surface.
Use a big tray so the potatoes are not crowded.
Add the onions later so they do not burn.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray at 200°C for 15 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Ruisleipa
steps: Mix 300 g of the rye flour, the lukewarm water, yeast, yoghurt and honey and leave to stand for 30 minutes.
Stir in the remaining rye flour, the white flour and the salt to a thick, sticky dough.
With wet hands shape into a flat round on a lined tray. Cover and leave to rise for 90 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220C. Prick the surface with a fork, brush with water and dust with rye flour.
Bake for 40 minutes until the loaf sounds hollow. Wrap in a damp cloth to cool.
current_recipe.description: A Finnish sour rye bread of rye flour, water and a starter, with a chewy crumb and a cracked crust, risen for 90 minutes and baked for 40 minutes.
tips: Do not knead the sticky dough.
Wet your hands to shape it.
Slice only when completely cold.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 5 days wrapped. Freeze sliced for 2 months.

current_recipe.title: Salmon Fillet with Dill Sauce
steps: Stir the soured cream, dill, lemon juice, mustard and a pinch of the salt together and chill.
Pat the salmon dry and season with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Fry skin-side down in the oil over a medium-high heat for 5 minutes without moving.
Turn and cook for 2 minutes more, then serve with the dill sauce.
current_recipe.description: Pan-fried salmon fillets served with a cool sauce of soured cream, dill, lemon and a little mustard.
tips: Pat the fish dry.
Do not move the fillets while the skin crisps.
Take it off the heat while the middle is just translucent.
Chill the sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Flake cold into a salad, with the sauce on the side.

current_recipe.title: Salmon Fish Cakes
steps: Poach the salmon in simmering water for 8 minutes, drain, cool and flake.
Dry the mash in the hot pan for 1 minute. Fold in the salmon, dill, lemon zest and juice, spring onions and salt. Shape into 8 patties.
Coat in the flour, egg and breadcrumbs and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the cakes for 6 minutes per side until golden.
current_recipe.description: Flaked salmon mixed with mashed potato, dill and lemon, shaped into patties, breadcrumbed and fried for 12 minutes.
tips: Dry the mash.
Fold gently to keep flakes.
If your pan runs hot, check at 4 minutes.
Chill before frying.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a hot oven so the crumb crisps.

current_recipe.title: Salmon Poke Bowls
ingredients: 400 g sushi-grade salmon fillet, farmed or previously frozen to kill parasites, skinless, cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar and honey. Toss half of it with the salmon and leave for 10 minutes in the fridge.
Spoon the sushi rice into four bowls.
Arrange the salmon, avocado, cucumber, edamame and pickled ginger on top in sections.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and scatter with the spring onions and sesame seeds. Serve at once.
current_recipe.description: Cubes of raw salmon in a soy and sesame dressing over sushi rice with avocado, cucumber, edamame and pickled ginger.
tips: Use fish sold for eating raw.
Keep it cold until the last moment.
Dress the fish only 10 minutes ahead.
Eat it the same day.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Do not keep leftovers that contain raw fish.

current_recipe.title: Salted Caramel Cookies
steps: Beat the butter and both sugars for 2 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt. Chill the dough for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180C and line 2 trays. Flatten a tablespoon of dough in your palm, press in some caramel pieces, and seal the dough around them. Roll into 24 balls.
Place 5 cm apart. Bake for 12 minutes until the edges are golden.
Sprinkle with the flaky salt straight out of the oven and cool on the trays for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Chewy brown sugar cookies filled with soft caramel pieces and finished with flaky sea salt, baked for 12 minutes.
tips: Use firm caramel sweets, not sauce.
Seal the caramel completely inside the dough.
Add flaky salt while the cookies are hot.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Samoan Chop Suey
ingredients: 400 g boneless chicken thighs, sliced thinly
2 carrots, about 200 g, cut into matchsticks
steps: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until browned. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the carrots and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes. Pour in the soy sauce, oyster sauce and water.
Add the noodles, toss for 2 minutes until they absorb the sauce, and serve at once.
current_recipe.description: A quick stir-fry of chicken, glass noodles, cabbage and carrot in a soy and ginger sauce, the way it is served at Samoan gatherings.
tips: Cut the chicken against the grain so it stays tender.
Do not soak the noodles for longer than the packet says, or they turn mushy.
Taste before serving; the soy may be enough salt.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Apple Crisp
ingredients: 1.2 kg apples, peeled and sliced 5 mm thick
1 tsp ground cinnamon, for the topping
steps: Heat the oven to 190C. Toss the apples with the caster sugar, lemon juice, cornflour and 1 tsp cinnamon. Spread in a single layer on a 33 by 45 cm rimmed tray.
Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and salt. Rub in the butter until crumbly.
Squeeze handfuls of the topping into clumps and scatter over the apples.
Bake for 35 minutes until the apples are tender and the topping is golden.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into 12 squares.
current_recipe.description: Sliced apples under a buttery oat topping, spread on a large tray and baked for 35 minutes for a crisp crust on every portion.
tips: Slice the apples evenly at 5 mm.
Squeeze the topping into clumps.
Rest before cutting.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in the oven.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Breakfast Hash
ingredients: 700 g potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 220C with a large tray inside. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp of the oil, paprika and salt.
Tip the potatoes onto the hot tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Add the pepper, onion, sausage and the remaining oil. Stir and roast for 12 minutes more, until the potatoes are golden.
Make 4 wells in the hash and crack an egg into each. Roast for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with the chives and serve from the tray.
current_recipe.description: Diced potatoes, peppers, onion and sausage roasted on one tray at 220C, with eggs baked into the hash for the last 8 minutes.
tips: Preheat the tray so the potatoes sizzle.
Spread the hash in a single layer.
Check the eggs at 6 minutes.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. The hash keeps for 2 days in the fridge without the eggs.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients: 800 g potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks
