steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large tray inside. Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons of the oil and half the salt, tip onto the hot tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Pat the chicken dry and rub with the remaining oil, the paprika, garlic powder, the remaining salt and the pepper.
Turn the potatoes, nestle the chicken skin side up among them and roast for 40 minutes, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear.
Squeeze over the lemon, scatter with the parsley and serve straight from the tray.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs and potato chunks roasted on one tray with paprika and garlic until golden. Four servings in 55 minutes.
tips: Give the potatoes a head start on the hot tray.
Dry the chicken skin thoroughly before seasoning.
Use two trays rather than crowding one.
Check the chicken at 35 minutes if your oven runs hot.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray at 200°C for 15 minutes to crisp the potatoes.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Chicken Parmesan
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, about 600 g, sliced in half horizontally
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and set a rack over a tray. Season the chicken with the salt.
Mix the panko, parmesan, oregano and olive oil. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then press into the crumb mixture.
Lay the cutlets on the rack and bake for 15 minutes.
Spoon 2 tbsp of tomato sauce over each cutlet and top with mozzarella. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the chicken reads 74C.
Warm the rest of the sauce and serve with the chicken, scattered with basil.
current_recipe.description: Breaded chicken breasts baked on a tray at 220C for 25 minutes with tomato sauce and mozzarella, no frying required.
tips: Pound the chicken to an even thickness.
Add the sauce and cheese late to keep the crumb crisp.
Use a rack so the underside crisps.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat in a 190C oven for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Cod and Vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 220C. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp of the oil and half the salt on a large tray. Roast for 15 minutes.
Add the green beans and tomatoes with the remaining oil and stir. Roast for 5 minutes.
Season the cod with the rest of the salt. Nestle the fillets among the vegetables and roast for 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Mix the butter, lemon zest and juice, garlic and parsley.
Spoon the lemon butter over the tray and serve straight away.
current_recipe.description: Cod fillets roasted on one tray with new potatoes, green beans and cherry tomatoes, with lemon butter spooned over before serving.
tips: Add the ingredients in stages, longest first.
Use thick fillets so they do not dry out.
Spoon the butter on at the end.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep for 1 day in the fridge.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Fish Tacos
ingredients: 600 g cod fillets, about 2.5 cm thick
steps: Heat the oven to 230C with a tray inside. Pat the fish dry and rub with the oil, chilli powder, cumin, garlic powder and half the salt.
Toss the cabbage, red onion and coriander with the juice of 1 lime and the remaining salt. Mix the soured cream with the juice of 1 lime.
Lay the fish on the hot tray and roast for 12 to 15 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side.
Flake the fish into the tortillas, top with the slaw and crema and serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.
current_recipe.description: White fish fillets seasoned with chilli and lime and roasted on a tray for 15 minutes, flaked into warm tortillas with slaw and crema.
tips: Choose thick fillets for large flakes.
Heat the tray before the fish goes on.
Dress the slaw just before serving.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Keep the components apart in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Nachos
ingredients: 60 g sliced jalapeños from a jar
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spread half the chips on a large lined tray.
Dot with half the beans, then scatter with half the cheese and half the jalapeños. Add the rest of the chips, beans, cheese and jalapeños.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and just browning at the edges.
Top with the spring onions, salsa, soured cream and coriander and serve straight from the tray.
current_recipe.description: Tortilla chips layered with beans, cheese and jalapeños on a tray and baked until bubbling. Four servings in 22 minutes.
tips: Build the nachos in two layers.
Grate the cheese yourself for a smoother melt.
Add the cold toppings after baking.
Check at 6 minutes if your oven runs hot.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. The chips soften within about 15 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Pork Chops
ingredients: 4 bone-in pork chops, about 1 kg, 2.5 cm thick
500 g sweet potatoes, cut into 2 cm chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 210C. Toss the sweet potato with 1 tbsp of the oil and half the salt on a large tray. Roast for 10 minutes.
Mix the mustard, thyme, 1 tbsp oil, pepper and remaining salt. Rub over the chops.
Add the chops, apples and onion to the tray with the remaining oil and stir the vegetables.
Roast for 15 minutes, turning the vegetables once, until the chops read 63C.
Rest for 5 minutes and spoon the apple and onion over the chops to serve.
current_recipe.description: Bone-in pork chops roasted with apple wedges, red onion and sweet potato on one tray for 25 minutes with thyme and mustard.
tips: Choose firm apples that hold their shape.
Cut the sweet potato small so it cooks in time.
Cook the chops to 63C and rest.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a 180C oven for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Vegetables
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, cut into 2.5 cm chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large tray inside. Toss the potatoes, peppers and onion with the oil, salt, mustard and thyme.
Tip onto the hot tray, add the sausages and roast for 15 minutes.
Turn the sausages, stir the vegetables and add the courgettes. Roast for 20 minutes more, until the sausages are browned and the vegetables are tender with dark edges.
current_recipe.description: Pork sausages roasted on one tray with peppers, red onion, courgette and potatoes until browned. Four servings in 45 minutes.
tips: Cut the potatoes a little smaller than the other vegetables.
Add the courgettes later so they do not collapse.
Do not crowd the tray.
Cut a sausage open to check it is cooked.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray at 200°C for 12 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Sheet Pan Shrimp Boil
ingredients: 2 corn cobs, about 500 g, cut into 4 pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes with half the Cajun seasoning, half the butter and the oil on a large tray and roast for 12 minutes.
Add the sausage and corn and roast for 8 minutes more.
Toss the prawns with the remaining seasoning and butter, nestle them on the tray and roast for 5 minutes until pink.
Squeeze over the lemon, scatter with the parsley and serve from the tray.
current_recipe.description: Prawns, sausage, sweetcorn and potatoes roasted on a tray with Cajun seasoning and butter.
tips: Cut the potatoes small.
Add the prawns last.
If your oven runs hot, check at 20 minutes in total.
Serve straight from the tray.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Do not keep shellfish leftovers.

current_recipe.title: Shrimp and Pepper Stir-Fry
ingredients: 480 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
300 g mixed bell peppers, cut into strips
steps: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, cornflour and water together in a small bowl.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the peppers and onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Push the vegetables aside, add the remaining oil and the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 2 minutes, turning once, until pink.
Pour in the sauce and toss everything for 1 minute, until glossy. Add the pepper and sesame oil and serve straight away.
current_recipe.description: Shrimp stir-fried with three colours of pepper, onion, garlic and ginger in a light low-sodium soy and rice vinegar sauce. Four servings in 18 minutes.
tips: Pat the shrimp very dry so that they sear instead of steaming.
Have the sauce and rice ready before the shrimp go in; there is no time to prepare once the pan is hot.
Cut large shrimp in half lengthwise for even cooking.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day; shrimp toughen on reheating, so eat the leftovers cold.

current_recipe.title: Skillet Gnocchi with Spinach
steps: Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes without moving. Turn and cook for 3 minutes more.
Push the gnocchi aside, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the spinach in handfuls until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the cream, water, nutmeg and salt. Bubble for 2 minutes, tossing, until the sauce coats the gnocchi.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and lemon juice and serve.
current_recipe.description: Shop-bought gnocchi crisped in a frying pan, then tossed with garlic, spinach, cream and parmesan.
tips: Cook the gnocchi in two batches if the pan is small.
Do not boil the gnocchi first.
Add crumbled goat cheese or bacon for variations.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Apple Crisp
ingredients: 1 kg apples, peeled, cored and sliced
steps: Toss the apples with the caster sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and cornflour in the slow cooker.
Rub the oats, flour, brown sugar, butter and salt together with your fingertips into a rough crumble and scatter over the apples.
Line the lid with a clean tea towel, cover and cook on low for 3 hours until the apples are tender.
Serve warm.
current_recipe.description: Sliced apples cooked on low under an oat, butter and brown sugar topping until soft and bubbling.
tips: Cut the apples thick.
Line the lid with a tea towel.
If your cooker runs hot, check at 2 hours 30 minutes.
Grill briefly for a crisper top.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in the microwave.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Apple Sauce
ingredients: 1.5 kg apples, peeled, cored and sliced
steps: Put the apples, water, sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 4 hours until completely soft.
Mash with a potato masher, or blend for a smooth sauce. Taste and add sugar if needed.
current_recipe.description: Apples cooked slowly with cinnamon and lemon until soft, then mashed into a chunky sauce.
tips: Use a mix of apples.
Do not add extra water.
No need to stir.
Taste before adding sugar.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Baked Beans
ingredients: 500 g dried haricot beans, soaked overnight and drained
steps: Put the beans, bacon and onion in the slow cooker.
Mix the tomatoes, tomato purée, treacle, sugar, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, water, salt and paprika. Pour over the beans and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, without lifting the lid, until the beans are completely tender.
If the sauce is thin, uncover, switch to high and cook for 30 minutes.
Stir and taste for seasoning before serving.
current_recipe.description: Dried haricot beans cooked on low for 8 hours in a molasses, tomato and mustard sauce with bacon until soft, sticky and sweet.
tips: Soak the beans overnight.
Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Reduce the sauce with the lid off if it is too thin.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Bean Soup
steps: Put the beans, bacon, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, water and bay leaves in the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 5 hours.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook for 2 hours more, until the beans are completely tender. If your slow cooker runs hot, check at 6 hours.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot, remove the bay leaves and taste for salt.
current_recipe.description: Dried haricot beans, ham, carrots and tomatoes cooked on low for 7 hours into a thick soup, with no soaking. Six servings.
tips: Check that the beans are fully tender before serving.
Add the tomatoes late.
Mash a few beans to thicken the soup.
Soak the beans overnight if you plan ahead.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days and thickens. Freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Beef Curry
ingredients: 800 g chuck steak, cut into 4 cm cubes
steps: Heat half the oil in a frying pan and brown the beef in two batches, 4 minutes each. Tip into the slow cooker.
Heat the rest of the oil and cook the onions for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute and add to the slow cooker.
Add the tomatoes, water, purée and salt. Cover and cook on low for 7 hours until the beef is tender. If your slow cooker runs hot, check at 6 hours.
Stir in the yogurt and coriander, taste for salt and serve.
current_recipe.description: Chuck steak simmered in a mild curry sauce of onion, tomato and spices for 7 hours on low. Four servings, with 15 minutes of work.
tips: Cook the curry powder in oil first.
Brown the beef before adding it.
Add the yogurt at the end, off the high heat.
Serve with plenty of rice to take up the sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming throughout.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Butter Chicken
ingredients: 900 g chicken thighs, boneless, cut into chunks
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger, garlic, garam masala, turmeric, chilli and salt. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Put the chicken and marinade in the slow cooker. Stir in the tomato purée, passata and sugar.
Cover and cook on low for 5 hours until the chicken is very tender.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the butter and cream and leave for 10 minutes.
Crush the fenugreek over the top, scatter with the coriander and serve.
current_recipe.description: Chicken thighs in a spiced tomato and butter sauce cooked on low for 5 hours, finished with cream and fenugreek.
tips: Marinate the chicken for the best flavour.
Add the dairy at the end.
Crush the fenugreek leaves before adding.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Cheesecake
ingredients: 500 g full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
steps: Mix the crumbs and melted butter and press into a lined 18 cm springform tin. Wrap the outside in a double layer of foil.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the soured cream, vanilla, lemon juice and flour.
Pour onto the base. Set the tin on a foil collar in the slow cooker and add 250 ml hot water around it.
Cover and cook on high for 90 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off, leave inside with the lid ajar for 1 hour, then chill for at least 6 hours.
current_recipe.description: A creamy vanilla cheesecake baked in a springform tin inside the slow cooker for 90 minutes, then chilled for 6 hours.
tips: Check the tin fits before you start.
Do not open the lid while it cooks.
Cool it slowly in the pot.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Chili
ingredients: 480 g tinned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and brown the mince for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, then the chili powder and cumin for 1 minute. Drain off any excess fat.
Tip into the slow cooker with the tomatoes, beans, purée, stock and salt and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours. If your slow cooker runs hot, check at 5 hours.
Stir, taste for salt and, if the chili is thin, cook uncovered on high for 20 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Beef mince, kidney beans, tomatoes and chili powder cooked together on low for 6 hours. Six servings, with 15 minutes of work.
tips: Brown the mince before it goes in.
Keep the stock modest; the pot does not reduce.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes to thicken.
Make it a day ahead for the best flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming throughout.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Lentil Soup
steps: Put the lentils, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, cumin, paprika, tomatoes, stock and bay leaves in the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until the lentils are tender. If your slow cooker runs hot, check at 5 hours.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the salt and lemon juice and taste.
Thin with hot water if the soup is too thick.
current_recipe.description: Brown lentils, carrots, celery and tomatoes cooked on low for 6 hours into a thick, spiced soup. Six servings, with 10 minutes of work.
tips: Rinse the lentils and check for grit.
Add the salt and lemon at the end.
Thin with hot water; the soup thickens as it stands.
Fry the vegetables first if you have time.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Freezes for up to 3 months. Loosen with water when reheating.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Meatballs
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. Mix with the beef, pork, egg, garlic, parmesan and salt until just combined. Shape into 24 balls.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and brown the meatballs in batches, 5 minutes each. Lift into the slow cooker.
Mix the tomatoes, purée and oregano and pour over.
Cover and cook on low for 4 hours, until the meatballs are cooked through. If your slow cooker runs hot, check at 3 hours.
current_recipe.description: Beef and pork meatballs simmered in tomato sauce on low for 4 hours until tender. Six servings, with 20 minutes of work.
tips: Brown the meatballs for a better texture and flavour.
Do not stir during the first 2 hours.
Keep them in one or two layers under the sauce.
Cut one open to check it is cooked through.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days in the sauce. Freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming throughout.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Oatmeal
steps: Grease the slow cooker. Add the oats, water, milk, sugar, cinnamon and salt and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours.
Stir well, stir in the vanilla and loosen with a splash of warm milk if needed. Serve hot.
current_recipe.description: Steel-cut oats cooked on low for seven hours in water and milk with cinnamon, ready and creamy when you wake.
tips: Use steel-cut oats, not rolled; rolled oats turn to mush.
Grease the pot generously.
Stir in the morning before serving.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Pasta
steps: Brown the sausage meat in a pan for 6 minutes, breaking it up. Put it in the slow cooker.
Add the onion, peppers, garlic, passata, stock, oregano, chilli flakes and salt. Cover and cook on low for 2 hours.
Stir in the penne, making sure it is below the surface. Switch to high and cook for 45 minutes, stirring once.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover and leave for 10 minutes until melted.
Scatter with the basil and serve.
current_recipe.description: Penne, Italian sausage, peppers and passata cooked together in the slow cooker for 3 hours with mozzarella melted through the top.
tips: Keep the pasta submerged in the sauce.
Add the pasta late so it does not turn to mush.
Loosen with hot stock if it gets too thick.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Add a splash of stock when reheating.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Peach Cobbler
ingredients: 800 g tinned peaches in juice, drained, syrup reserved
50 g caster sugar, for the topping
steps: Grease the slow cooker. Toss the peaches with 80 g sugar, the cornflour, cinnamon, vanilla and 4 tbsp of the reserved syrup. Spread in the cooker.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and 50 g sugar. Rub in the butter, then stir in the milk to a thick, sticky batter.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter over the peaches and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.
Lay a clean tea towel under the lid. Cover and cook on low for 3 hours until the topping is set.
Rest for 15 minutes and serve warm.
current_recipe.description: Sliced peaches under a sweet biscuit topping, slow cooked on low for 3 hours until bubbling and set, with cinnamon and vanilla.
tips: Put a tea towel under the lid.
Do not expect the topping to brown.
Rest before serving so the juices thicken.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in the microwave.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Pulled Beef
steps: Put the onion and garlic in the base of the slow cooker. Lay the beef on top.
Whisk the stock, tomato purée, vinegar, sugar, paprika, salt and pepper and pour over the beef.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Lift out the beef, shred with two forks and return to the juices. Stir, skim off any fat, and serve.
current_recipe.description: Beef chuck cooked on low in a smoky tomato and vinegar sauce for eight hours, then shredded to pile into buns.
tips: Do not lift the lid during cooking; it lets out heat.
Skim the fat from the juices before mixing in the meat.
Taste at the end and adjust the salt and vinegar.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and freezes for up to 3 months.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Risotto
steps: Melt the 40 g butter in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains turn translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine and let it sizzle away. Tip the rice into the slow cooker.
Add the hot stock, salt and pepper and stir once.
Cover and cook on high for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the rice is tender with a slight bite.
Stir in the parmesan and cubed butter vigorously for 1 minute, scatter with parsley and serve.
current_recipe.description: Arborio rice, stock, onion, white wine and parmesan cooked on high for 2 hours 30 minutes in the slow cooker into a creamy risotto.
tips: Use arborio rice for a creamy result.
Do not lift the lid before 2 hours.
Add a splash of hot stock if it sets.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Leftover risotto makes good rice cakes.

current_recipe.title: Slow Cooker Sticky Toffee Pudding
ingredients: 150 g dark brown sugar, for the sauce
steps: Soak the dates in the boiling water with the bicarbonate of soda for 10 minutes. Grease a 1.5 litre heatproof basin.
Beat the 60 g butter and 150 g sugar for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, vanilla and the dates with their liquid.
Pour into the basin and cover with pleated foil. Set on a trivet in the slow cooker and add hot water halfway up the basin.
Cover and cook on high for 2 hours 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Simmer the sauce butter, sugar and cream for 5 minutes. Turn out the pudding and pour over half the sauce.
current_recipe.description: A steamed date sponge cooked for 2 hours 30 minutes in the slow cooker and served with a hot toffee sauce.
tips: Soak the dates with bicarbonate of soda.
Pleat the foil to allow for rising.
Serve with a jug of extra sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in the microwave.

current_recipe.title: Soba Noodle Salad
ingredients: 1 cucumber, about 200 g, cut into matchsticks
2 carrots, about 120 g, cut into matchsticks
steps: Boil the soba for 6 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold running water and rub gently until the water runs clear.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey and ginger.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, then fold in the cucumber, carrot and spring onions.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and serve cold.
current_recipe.description: Cold buckwheat noodles with cucumber, carrot, spring onion and sesame seeds in a soy and rice vinegar dressing.
tips: Rinse and rub the noodles.
Cut the vegetables thin.
Dress while the noodles are damp.
Chill for 15 minutes for a colder salad.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

current_recipe.title: Sol Kadhi
steps: Soak the kokum in the warm water for 10 minutes. Squeeze it to release the colour and sourness, then strain, keeping the liquid.
Blend the coconut milk with the garlic, green chilli and cumin until smooth.
Stir in the kokum liquid, salt and sugar. Taste and adjust.
Chill for 30 minutes and serve topped with the coriander.
current_recipe.description: A pink, cooling drink of coconut milk infused with dried kokum, garlic, green chilli and coriander, served chilled.
tips: Taste the kokum soaking water; if it is weak, add a little more kokum.
Serve it cold, not iced, so it does not water down.
Skip the garlic if you prefer a milder drink.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Stir before serving.

current_recipe.title: Soupe Aux Choux
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot for 6 minutes until the fat runs. Add the onion and carrots and cook for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add half the cabbage, the potatoes, stock, bay leaves and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook for 35 minutes.
Add the rest of the cabbage and cook for 20 minutes more until tender.
Crush a few potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken, taste for salt and stir in the parsley.
current_recipe.description: A thick winter soup of cabbage, potato, carrot and smoked bacon, simmered for 60 minutes in stock.
tips: Add the cabbage in two stages for body and bite.
Taste for salt only at the end; bacon is salty.
Crush a few potatoes to thicken the soup.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: South African Pap
steps: For the gravy, heat the oil and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, sugar, salt and water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring the water and salt to a boil. Pour in the maize meal in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Lower the heat, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring from the bottom every 5 minutes, until thick and stiff.
Spoon onto plates and serve with the gravy.
current_recipe.description: Stiff maize meal porridge cooked until it holds its shape, served with a tomato and onion gravy.
tips: Add the maize meal slowly.
Use a heavy pot to prevent sticking.
Serve with boerewors for a braai meal.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Slice and pan-cook leftovers.

current_recipe.title: Spaghetti al Limone
steps: Boil the spaghetti in salted water until 1 minute short of done. Keep 250 ml of the water.
Melt the butter in a wide pan with the lemon zest, add 100 ml of the pasta water and bubble for 1 minute.
Add the spaghetti and toss for 1 minute.
Take off the heat and add the lemon juice and most of the Parmesan, tossing, with more water until creamy.
Serve with the pepper and the remaining Parmesan.
current_recipe.description: Spaghetti in a sharp, creamy sauce of lemon juice and zest, butter and Parmesan, ready in 20 minutes.
tips: Add the juice and cheese off the heat.
Toss constantly so the sauce turns creamy.
Use pasta water to loosen the sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh.

current_recipe.title: Spaghetti alla Norma
ingredients: 600 g aubergines, cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Toss the aubergine with the salt and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan and fry the aubergine in 2 batches for 8 minutes each until deep golden. Remove.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and chilli to the pan for 1 minute, then the tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water for 1 minute less than the pack says. Reserve a mug of the water and drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and aubergine and a splash of water. Serve with the ricotta salata and basil.
current_recipe.description: Spaghetti with fried aubergine, tomato sauce, basil and ricotta salata, a Sicilian dish from Catania, ready in 1 hour 10 minutes.
tips: Salt and dry the aubergine before frying.
Brown the aubergine properly.
Use ricotta salata, or feta if unavailable.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Spaghetti Frittata
steps: Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, parsley, pepper and salt. Stir in the spaghetti and leave for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Pour in the mixture and press flat.
Cook for 8 minutes until the base is golden and the top is nearly set.
Slide onto a plate, invert back into the pan and cook for 4 minutes more. Rest for 3 minutes and cut into wedges.
current_recipe.description: Leftover cooked spaghetti mixed with eggs, cheese and parsley and set into a round cake in a pan. Four servings in 30 minutes.
tips: Use a non-stick pan so the frittata slides out.
Finish under a hot grill instead of flipping if you prefer.
Let the mixture rest so the pasta absorbs the egg.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Eat cold or reheat in a pan.

current_recipe.title: Spinach Stuffed Chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Wilt the spinach with the garlic and olive oil, cool, squeeze dry and chop. Mix with the cream cheese, parmesan and pepper.
Cut a deep pocket in each breast, fill with the spinach mixture and secure with cocktail sticks. Season with the salt.
Brown the chicken in the vegetable oil in an ovenproof pan for 3 minutes per side.
Cook in the oven for 22 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes and remove the sticks.
current_recipe.description: Chicken breasts filled with spinach, cream cheese and garlic, wrapped in nothing but their own skin of seasoning and cooked for 30 minutes.
tips: Squeeze the spinach dry.
Keep the pocket opening small.
If your oven runs hot, check at 18 minutes.
Rest before slicing.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat gently.

current_recipe.title: Strawberry Syrup
steps: Simmer the strawberries, sugar, water and lemon juice over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, skimming the foam.
Mash the fruit lightly, then strain through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp gently.
Pour into a clean bottle and cool.
current_recipe.description: A bright red syrup of strawberries, sugar, water and lemon, for milk, soda, pancakes and ice cream.
tips: Skim the foam.
Press the pulp gently.
If your hob runs hot, keep the heat low.
Simmer longer for a thicker syrup.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

current_recipe.title: Taquitos
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a tray. Warm the tortillas wrapped in a damp tea towel for 30 seconds.
Mix the chicken, cream cheese, cheddar, salsa and cumin.
Spoon the filling down the middle of each tortilla and roll up tightly. Set seam side down on the tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Serve with the sour cream.
current_recipe.description: Corn tortillas rolled around shredded chicken, cream cheese and cheddar and baked until crisp.
tips: Warm the tortillas first.
Roll tightly.
If your oven runs hot, check at 15 minutes.
Set seam side down.
current_recipe.storage: Best warm. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days and reheats in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Tequenos
ingredients: 400 g firm white cheese (halloumi or queso blanco), cut into 20 sticks
steps: Mix the flour, egg, butter, sugar, salt and water and knead to a smooth dough. Wrap and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin, about 1 mm. Cut into 20 strips, 3 cm wide and 25 cm long.
Wrap each strip around a cheese stick in a spiral, sealing the ends with a dab of water.
Heat the oil to 180°C. Fry the tequeños in batches for 2 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
current_recipe.description: Sticks of salty white cheese wrapped in thin dough and cooked until golden and crisp, a Venezuelan party snack.
tips: Seal the ends properly.
Freeze the cheese sticks for 15 minutes first.
Freeze uncooked tequeños for up to 1 month.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten hot. Uncooked tequeños freeze for 1 month.

current_recipe.title: Thai Peanut Noodles
ingredients: 1/2 cucumber, about 150 g, sliced into strips
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey, garlic and chilli, then whisk in the warm water until pourable.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, about 5 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, carrot, cucumber and spring onions.
Top with the peanuts and coriander.
current_recipe.description: Rice noodles tossed in a sauce of peanut butter, soy sauce, lime and chilli with carrot, cucumber and coriander.
tips: Add the water slowly.
Rinse the noodles in cold water.
Taste and add more lime for a sharper sauce.
Keep a spoon of sauce back to loosen leftovers.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Loosen with a splash of water before serving.

current_recipe.title: Tian Provencal
ingredients: 1 aubergine, about 300 g, sliced 5 mm thick
2 courgettes, about 400 g, sliced 5 mm thick
4 tomatoes, about 500 g, sliced 5 mm thick
steps: Heat the oven to 190C. Cook the onions in 1 tbsp of the oil for 12 minutes until soft and golden, adding the garlic for the last minute. Spread in a 25 cm dish.
Sprinkle the aubergine and courgette slices with half the salt, leave for 15 minutes and pat dry.
Stand the aubergine, courgette and tomato slices on edge in the dish in alternating overlapping rows, packing them tightly.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and scatter over the thyme, the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 20 minutes more until the edges are browned.
current_recipe.description: Overlapping slices of courgette, aubergine, tomato and onion baked in a dish with olive oil and thyme for 45 minutes.
tips: Salt the aubergine and courgette and pat them dry first.
Slice everything to the same thickness for even cooking.
Pack the slices tightly; they shrink as they bake.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat at 180C for 10 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Trenette al Pesto
ingredients: 150 g green beans, cut in 3 cm lengths
steps: Blend the basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheeses and salt, adding the oil in a thin stream, to a rough paste.
Boil the potatoes in a large pan of salted water for 5 minutes. Add the beans and boil for 3 minutes more.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, about 8 minutes. Keep 150 ml of the water, then drain.
Toss everything with the pesto and enough of the water to make it creamy.
current_recipe.description: Flat ribbon pasta cooked with potato and green beans and tossed in fresh basil pesto, made in 25 minutes.
tips: Never heat the pesto.
Cook the potatoes and beans in the same water.
Add pasta water to loosen the sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Best fresh. The pesto keeps for 3 days under oil.

current_recipe.title: Trinidadian Pelau
ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs on the bone, skinned
steps: Mix the chicken with the green seasoning and salt and leave for 30 minutes.
Heat the sugar and oil in a heavy pot until it melts and turns dark amber, 3 to 4 minutes. Add the chicken and stir for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, garlic and carrots and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the scotch bonnet, pigeon peas and rice for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes.
Remove the scotch bonnet, fluff, and scatter with the coriander.
current_recipe.description: Chicken browned in caramelised sugar and cooked with rice, pigeon peas, carrots and coconut milk into a one-pot Sunday dish.
tips: Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Stand back when adding chicken to the sugar.
Serve with coleslaw.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water.

current_recipe.title: Tuna Poke Bowls
ingredients: 400 g tuna steak, sold for eating raw, cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Stir the rice vinegar through the cooled sushi rice and divide between four bowls.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil and honey and toss with the tuna just before serving.
Arrange the tuna, mango, cucumber, radish and nori on the rice.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and serve with the lime wedges.
current_recipe.description: Cubes of raw tuna in a soy and sesame dressing over sushi rice with mango, cucumber, radish and seaweed.
tips: Use tuna sold for eating raw.
Keep it cold.
Dress it at the last moment.
Cool the rice first.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten straight away. Do not keep leftovers that contain raw fish.

current_recipe.title: Turkish Meatballs
steps: Mix the lamb, beef, grated onion, parsley, cumin, paprika, breadcrumbs and salt and knead for 2 minutes. Chill for 20 minutes.
Shape into 12 ovals and press slightly flat.
Heat the grill to high and cook the kofte for 12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes.
Stir the garlic into the yoghurt. Serve the kofte in the flatbreads with the tomato, onion, sumac and yoghurt.
current_recipe.description: Lamb and beef kofte flavoured with cumin, paprika and parsley, grilled for 12 minutes and served with yoghurt and flatbread.
tips: Squeeze the grated onion dry.
Chill the mixture before shaping.
If your grill runs hot, check at 9 minutes.
Do not press them too thin.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan.

current_recipe.title: Turon
steps: Cut each banana in half lengthways, then in half crosswise to make 8 pieces. Roll each piece in about 1 tablespoon of brown sugar.
Place a banana piece on the corner of a wrapper, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and seal the edge with a little water.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a small, deep pan. Cook the turon in 2 batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep gold and the sugar has caramelised.
Drain on kitchen paper, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve warm.
current_recipe.description: Banana halves rolled in brown sugar and spring roll wrappers, then cooked until the sugar melts into a crisp caramel shell.
tips: Keep the wrappers under a damp cloth.
Do not let the oil get too hot.
Seal the seams firmly so the sugar does not leak.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten warm. Keeps for 1 day and crisps in a hot oven.

current_recipe.title: Vegan Cupcakes
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 12-hole muffin tin. Stir the vinegar into the 250 ml oat milk and leave for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, caster sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt.
Whisk the soured oat milk with the oil and 1 tsp of the vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and fold until just combined.
Divide between the cases at once and bake for 22 minutes. Cool completely.
Beat the vegan block, icing sugar, 2 tbsp oat milk and remaining vanilla until fluffy and swirl onto the cupcakes.
current_recipe.description: Light vanilla cupcakes made with oat milk, oil and a splash of vinegar, topped with a vegan buttercream, baked for 22 minutes.
tips: Bake the batter immediately after mixing.
Use a firm vegan baking block for the buttercream.
Frost only when cool.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container for 3 days.

current_recipe.title: Vegetable Wellington
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the squash with half the oil for 20 minutes.
While the squash roasts, fry the mushrooms and onion in the remaining oil for 10 minutes until dry. Wilt the spinach for 2 minutes, then squeeze it very dry and chop.
Mix the squash, mushrooms, spinach, chestnuts, thyme and salt. Cool completely.
Pile the filling down the middle of the pastry on a lined tray, brush the edges with egg, fold over, seal and score the top. Brush with egg.
Bake on a hot tray for 30 minutes until deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes.
current_recipe.description: Roasted butternut squash, mushrooms, spinach and chestnuts wrapped in puff pastry and baked until golden.
tips: Cook the filling until dry.
Cool it completely.
If your oven runs hot, check at 24 minutes.
Slice with a serrated knife.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven for 20 minutes.

current_recipe.title: Veloute de Champignons
steps: Melt half the butter in a large pan and cook the mushrooms in two batches for 10 minutes each until deep golden and dry. Set a few slices aside.
Return all the mushrooms to the pan with the remaining butter, the shallot and the garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then add the stock gradually, stirring. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth. Stir in the cream, lemon juice, salt and pepper and warm through.
Serve with the reserved mushrooms on top.
current_recipe.description: A smooth cream of mushroom soup made with butter, flour, stock and cream and blended until velvety, ready in 35 minutes.
tips: Cook the mushrooms until they are dry and deeply browned.
Add the stock gradually so the soup stays smooth.
Finish with lemon to lift the flavour.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat gently and do not boil.

current_recipe.title: White Bean Chili
steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano and ground coriander and stir for 1 minute.
Add the green chillies, two thirds of the beans, the sweetcorn, stock and salt.
Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mash the remaining beans and stir into the chili. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the lime juice and coriander and serve with the soured cream.
current_recipe.description: Cannellini beans, sweetcorn and green chillies simmered in vegetable stock with cumin and oregano for 30 minutes into a pale, creamy meat-free chili.
tips: Mash some beans to thicken the chili.
Bloom the spices in oil first.
Add the lime at the end.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

current_recipe.title: Witch Finger Cookies
steps: Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale. Beat in the egg, vanilla and almond extract.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt to a soft dough. Cover and chill for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Roll tablespoons of dough into fingers 8 cm long. Pinch two knuckles in each, score lines with a knife and press an almond into the tip.
Bake on lined trays for 15 minutes until pale gold. Cool, then lift each almond and dab a little jam underneath before pressing back.
current_recipe.description: Buttery almond shortbread cookies shaped like long, crooked fingers, with an almond for a fingernail and a smear of jam for gore.
tips: Press the almonds in firmly so they stay attached.
Chill the shaped dough so the shapes hold.
Cool the cookies fully before adding the jam.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight tin for 5 days.

current_recipe.title: Yorkshire Pudding Wraps
steps: Whisk the eggs, flour, milk and salt until smooth and leave for 20 minutes. Heat the oven to 220°C.
Divide the oil among 4 wide, shallow holes of a tin or 4 small round tins and heat in the oven for 5 minutes until smoking.
Pour in the batter, shut the door and cook for 25 minutes without opening it.
Warm the gravy. Spread each pudding with horseradish, fill with beef and rocket, and fold. Serve with the gravy.
current_recipe.description: Large Yorkshire puddings cooked for 25 minutes in a hot tin and filled with sliced roast beef, gravy and horseradish. Four servings in 1 hour.
tips: Rest the batter before cooking.
Heat the oil until it smokes.
If your oven runs hot, check at 20 minutes.
Do not open the door while they rise.
current_recipe.storage: Best eaten at once. Cooked puddings keep in the fridge for 1 day; crisp in a hot oven.

current_recipe.title: Yuxiang Aubergine
ingredients: 2 aubergines, about 600 g, cut into 6 cm batons
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp cold water
steps: Toss the aubergine with the salt and leave for 15 minutes. Squeeze dry.
Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wok over a high heat and cook the aubergine for 6 minutes, turning, until soft and golden. Push to the side.
Add the remaining oil, the pork, chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and stock. Bubble for 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings.
Stir in the cornflour mixture, then the spring onions.
current_recipe.description: Aubergine strips simmered until silky in a sweet, sour and spicy Sichuan sauce of chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger, with a little minced pork.
tips: Use long, thin aubergines if you can find them.
Doubanjiang is salty; taste before adding extra salt.
Leave out the pork for a vegetarian version, adding a tablespoon of soy sauce.
current_recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently.
